Article Title: Nepal faces days of rain, snow and storms as Cyclone Arnab wreaks havoc in India
Article Text:
Cyclone Arnab (Representational Image)

NEW DELHI: Cyclone ‘Arnab’ has battered India’s eastern coast, uprooting trees and electric poles, damaging roads and bringing torrential rain, with some areas of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha recording up to 30 cm of rainfall. The storm’s impact is now expected to extend to Nepal, which is bracing for several days of rain, thunderstorms and snowfall from Thursday.The Nepal Meteorological Department’s Weather Forecasting Division said the country was currently experiencing the partial influence of westerly winds, with the approaching cyclone expected to bring widespread precipitation and a risk of heavy rain and snowfall through the weekend.“The country is currently under the partial influence of westerly winds. In addition, the country is expected to come under the influence of Cyclone ‘Arnab’, developed over the Bay of Bengal, from Kartik 12 (Thursday),” the department said in its latest bulletin.Weather conditions remained relatively clear in the Himalayan and hilly regions on Wednesday morning, although fog and mist affected parts of the Terai, valleys and river basins.The department forecast increasing cloud cover and scattered precipitation from Wednesday afternoon, with conditions becoming more unsettled overnight. Koshi, Madhesh, Bagmati, Gandaki and Lumbini provinces are among the areas expected to experience rain, while snowfall is possible in Himalayan regions.The risk is forecast to increase on Thursday night, when thunderstorms and lightning could accompany rain and snowfall. Heavy precipitation is possible in parts of Koshi, Bagmati and Gandaki provinces, while some areas of Lumbini could also receive heavy rainfall.Friday and Saturday are expected to bring the most widespread impacts. The department warned that heavy rain or snowfall could affect several provinces, with isolated locations facing the possibility of very heavy precipitation.Its Friday forecast states, “Mostly cloudy throughout the country. Light to moderate rain or snowfall accompanied by thunder and lightning is possible at most places in Koshi, Madhesh, Bagmati, Gandaki and Lumbini Provinces and at many places in Karnali and Sudurpashchim Provinces.”The expected combination of westerly winds and moisture associated with Cyclone Arnab could increase the risk of flooding in low-lying areas and landslides in vulnerable hilly regions. Heavy snowfall could also create hazardous conditions in high-altitude areas.Meanwhile, in India, at least three people died in cyclone Arnab-related incidents in Andhra Pradesh on Wednesday. South Coast Railway (SCoR) cancelled 57 trains and rescheduled 15 others as a precautionary measure. However, officials quoted by ANI said the cyclone had weakened from a very severe to a severe cyclonic storm after moving over land, and was expected to weaken further. Four additional NDRF teams were deployed to Andhra Pradesh.
Article Summary: Cyclone ‘Arnab’ has battered India’s eastern coast, uprooting trees and electric poles. Some areas of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha have recorded up to 30 cm of rainfall. The storm's impact is now expected to extend to Nepal, which is bracing for rain, thunderstorms and snowfall.

Article Title: 'Taking down Instagram accounts won't make questions disappear': Abhijeet Dipke accuses Centre of digital crackdown
Article Text:
CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke

NEW DELHI : Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Wednesday criticised the Centre over an alleged crackdown on anti-government posts and accounts on Instagram. He warned that silencing citizens by taking down content would not address the public grievances.On Wednsday, in a post on X, Dipke wrote, “The Instagram crackdown is not going to work!“The government is taking down thousands of posts and accounts every day, but it seems to be missing a fundamental point.“Instagram is just a platform where people are raising their questions. The reasons behind those questions exist far beyond social media, and taking down accounts won't make them disappear,” Dipke wrote, warning that the alleged censorship could further erode trust among the very people the government is supposed to answer to.His remarks come amid wider scrutiny of online content restrictions and freedom of expression. Activists and political groups have raised concerns over account suspensions and takedown directives, including those reportedly issued under Section 69A of the Information Technology Act.According to PTI, social media platforms including Meta and X have been asked by the Centre to restrict posts and handles raising questions on youth unemployment, governance, and public infrastructure.Critics argue that restricting online content does not address underlying concerns over unemployment, examination paper leaks, governance and public infrastructure.The issue has also reached the courts. On October 27, the Delhi High Court issued notice to the Centre and the concerned department on a petition challenging the withholding of the Instagram handle @bring_back__ballot in India.The account is associated with the “Bring Back Ballot” initiative of Mission Save Constitution and advocate Mehmood Pracha, its national convenor.The petition stated that the handle was withheld on October 10, the day organisers held a protest at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi. It displayed the message: “Account not available in India. This is because we complied with a legal request to restrict this content.”The petitioners alleged, “No notice, hearing, reasons or copy of any order was ever furnished to the Petitioners.”The initiative advocated a return to paper ballots under the slogan “EVM Hatao Desh Bachao”. The petition said organisers had informed Delhi Police about the protest on October 9.Justice Amit Mahajan issued notice and sought the Centre’s response. Central Government Standing Counsel Ashish Dixit accepted notice on behalf of the Ministry of Home Affairs, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology and the designated officer. Advocate Amee Rana accepted notice for Meta Platforms.The matter is listed for hearing on November 6, when the court is expected to consider the petition further.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke criticised the Centre over an alleged crackdown on anti-government posts and accounts on Instagram. He warned that silencing citizens by taking down content would not address the public grievances.

Article Title: Mercedes crash: Kochi police commissioner removed from post after accident involving judge’s minor son; 4 cops suspended
Article Text:
Kochi City Police Commissioner Kaliraj Mahesh Kumar has been transferred, along with the suspension of four personnel.





Kochi: The Keralam govt has removed S. Kaliraj Mahesh Kumar as Kochi City District Police Chief amid mounting allegations of police lapses in the handling of the Cheranalloor fatal car crash case, in which a 55-year-old man was killed by a speeding luxury car allegedly driven by the 17-year-old son of an additional judge.Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan signed the order on Wednesday , acting on a recommendation from the Home Department. R. Nishanthini, currently serving as IGP (South Zone), is likely to succeed Kumar, who is yet to be given a new posting.The removal follows the suspension on Tuesday of four officers attached to the Cheranalloor police station. The suspended officers are station house officer and sub-inspector Viswajith V S, circle inspector Syam Kumar K S, grade ASI Manoj K T and senior civil police officer Arun Joshy. Jayabalakrishnan, who ran a roadside eatery, was reportedly heading home when the accident occurred around 2.20 am.Home minister Ramesh Chennithala had told the assembly that there had been serious police lapses and that he had personally reprimanded the director general of police after learning that the FIR had not initially included the charge of culpable homicide. A team of officers led by ADGP (law and order) P Vijayan visited the accident site and the victim’s family in Kochi on Tuesday, as directed by the minister.Vijayan held discussions with senior Kochi city police officers, including commissioner Kaliraj Mahesh Kumar, for nearly two hours on Tuesday. He also visited the accident site at Maraparambu on Container Road and briefly spoke to a watchman who was present at the spot. Both Ramesh and Vijayan said the law would take its course irrespective of persons involved.Addressing media, Vijayan had said that the police had already moved the court seeking to revoke the bail granted to the juvenile by the concerned magistrate. When asked about the possibility of an arrest of the judge, as he was arrayed as an accused, he said that it was a matter that involved multiple legal formalities, including obtaining the requisite permission from the judiciary.Meanwhile, the arrival of a separate team from the state capital is widely interpreted as a sign of the authorities' dissatisfaction with the city police's handling of the investigation.The family of the victim had also staged another protest at the station on Monday night, but called it off after Ramesh assured a fair investigation. They had warned that they would resume the protest if their demands were not met by 4 pm on Tuesday.Meanwhile, an overnight search at the judge's apartment in Aluva continued for several hours until Wednesday morning. Police have collected CCTV footage from the premises and seized documents relating to the luxury car involved in the crash and a premium motorcycle. Footage purportedly showing the car being driven out of the apartment had earlier circulated widely on social media.The police had initially registered a case against the minor driver under Sections 281 and 106(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), relating to rash driving and causing death by a rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide. The teenager was subsequently released on station bail under Section 8 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015.Jayabalakrishnan, who ran a roadside eatery, was heading home after closing the shop when the accident occurred at 2.20 am on Sunday. Both vehicles were travelling towards Kalamassery.Police had evidence that the car had travelled at over 100 kmph sometime before the accident, and Section 105 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder) and charges for speeding were added. The juvenile who was sent home on Monday morning was later picked up again after an additional section was added.
Article Summary: S. Kaliraj Mahesh Kumar has been transferred, along with the suspension of four personnel. Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan signed the order on Wednesday, acting on a recommendation from the Home Department. The removal follows the suspension on Tuesday of four officers attached to the Cheranalloor police station.

Article Title: Prayagraj’s cultural, literary legacy celebrated at JNU festival
Article Text:
Over 450 people gathered to celebrate Prayagraj's cultural and intellectual heritage at Jawaharlal Nehru University.

NEW DELHI: From its centuries-old traditions of learning and literature to its cultural and spiritual identity, Prayagraj’s legacy took centre stage at Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU), where over 450 people with connections to the city gathered for ‘Prayag Utsav 2026’.Organised by Shankh Initiatives as part of ‘Prayag-Delhi Sangam 2026’, the festival brought together academics, writers, artists, professionals and former residents of Prayagraj living in Delhi-NCR. The event, held at JNU’s Convention Centre, featured discussions on the city’s intellectual history, literary contributions and contemporary cultural identity.Addressing the valedictory session, Uttar Pradesh cabinet minister Nand Gopal Gupta ‘Nandi’ said Prayagraj’s identity extended beyond its geographical boundaries, connecting people through shared memories and traditions.Referring to the confluence of the Ganga, Yamuna and the traditionally revered Saraswati, he said the city’s spiritual and intellectual heritage continued to influence generations. He also acknowledged the efforts of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah and UP chief minister Yogi Adityanath in promoting India’s cultural heritage.Former UP minister Siddharth Nath Singh, who inaugurated the festival, said such initiatives helped connect Prayagraj’s literary and cultural traditions with contemporary academic discourse.He emphasised the importance of engaging younger generations with their cultural roots.Professor Anand Shankar Singh, principal of Iswar Saran Degree College, described Prayagraj’s intellectual heritage as a living tradition that continued to shape contemporary thought.Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University vice-chancellor Murli Manohar Pathak also spoke on India’s knowledge traditions.Two panel discussions examined Prayagraj’s historical significance and contributions to education and literature. Kathak performances, folk music, poetry recitations and musical presentations formed the cultural programme, bringing together different generations with enduring ties to the city.
Article Summary: Over 450 people gathered to celebrate Prayagraj's cultural and intellectual heritage at Jawaharlal Nehru University. The event featured discussions on the city’s intellectual history, literary contributions and contemporary cultural identity. Kathak performances, folk music, poetry recitations and musical presentations formed the cultural programme.

Article Title: 'Process becomes punishment in our system': Ex-SC judge Sanjay Kaul on Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam bail pleas
Article Text:
Ex-SC judge Justice Kaul flags ‘punishment’ of prolonged custody before conviction

‘Met him only a couple of times’: Justice Kaul on Saurav Das

NEW DELHI: Former Supreme Court judge Sanjay Kishan Kaul has said that the period before conviction or acquittal has become a "punishment" in India, commenting on the denial of bail to Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam . He said that prolonged legal proceedings can themselves become a form of punishment and that bail should generally be the norm.In an interview with news agency ANI, Kaul said he had generally taken a liberal view on bail, but acknowledged that certain laws explicitly restrict the granting of bail in specific cases."I have taken a generally very liberal view on bail. I feel the bail cannot be the punishment. The conviction is the punishment. In our system, unfortunately, the pre-conviction or acquittal period itself becomes a punishment. The process becomes a punishment," former Supreme Court judge said.Kaul said several judges had raised concerns about the issue. He also referred to a judgment written by Justice Sundaresh, with whom he had dealt with the question of bail and the principles governing custody."And many judges have been writing and talking about it. In fact, I, sitting with Justice Sundaresh, had dealt elaborately with the bail itself, trying to say, why are you people under custody? Justice Sundaresh wrote the judgment.He's, to my mind, a liberal judge on this. And we tried to lay down norms, etc., which were already in existence, but trying to, you know, until this case. So in most cases, our view is, that bail should be the norm. But there are certain acts which prohibit bail," said Kaul.Kaul has co-authored an upcoming memoir, Without Fear or Favour, with Jay Vinayak Ojha. The book is scheduled for release on October 31.Khalid and Imam are accused under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) in connection with an alleged larger conspiracy behind the February 2020 northeast Delhi riots. According to the prosecution, the violence left 53 people dead and more than 700 injured.The riots broke out amid protests against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019, and the proposed National Register of Citizens.On January 5 this year, the Supreme Court denied bail to Khalid and Imam in the case related to the alleged conspiracy behind the 2020 riots. In its judgment, the court observed that the two accused stood on a "qualitatively different footing" in terms of the prosecution's case and the evidence against them.In September, the Delhi high court had also rejected their bail pleas. The case stems from FIR 59/2020, registered by the Delhi Police Special Cell to investigate the alleged larger conspiracy behind the February 2020 northeast Delhi riots.Meanwhile, former Supreme Court judge Justice Sanjay Kishan Kaul also clarified his association with Cockroach Janta Party activist Saurav Das, saying he had met him only a couple of times when Das was working as a journalist and had advised him to "taper down a little" in his language.Justice Kaul told news agency ANI that a photograph of him with Das, taken at a Diwali gathering about a year ago, was being used to suggest that he shared a particular ideology."So, it was one year ago. He was not even in the news then," Justice Kaul said, explaining how the meeting came about."He was a journalist, maybe met me a couple of times. He was insistent that I must, at Diwali time, come. I was going somewhere else. I said, 'Okay, I'll drop in for ten minutes.' I told my wife, 'Have a cup of coffee, I'll drop in for ten minutes, and then we'll go.' That's all that happened," he said.Asked whether he had mentored Das at any point, Justice Kaul denied doing so, while acknowledging that he had advised the activist on his choice of words."I was not mentoring him, but once or twice he met me, I told him that, I will always tell you to taper down a little in your language," he said.Justice Kaul added that differences in language and expression across generations could sometimes cause discomfort, particularly among those accustomed to more civil forms of conversation.
Article Summary: Former Supreme Court judge Sanjay Kishan Kaul says prolonged legal proceedings can themselves become a form of punishment. Kaul said he had generally taken a liberal view on bail, but acknowledged that certain laws explicitly restrict the granting of bail in specific cases. He also clarified his association with Cockroach Janta Party activist Saurav Das.

Article Title: Centre deputes a high-level team to investigate death of Cheetah, caused by firearm pellet injuries, in Madhya Pradesh
Article Text:
19-month-old radio-collared male cheetah, an offspring of Namibia-born Cheetah Nirva, was found injured on Oct 25

NEW DELHI: The Centre on Wednesday deputed a high-level team to investigation the death of a 19-month-old male Cheetah of Kuno National Park, Madhya Pradesh, caused by firearm pellet injuries.The team has been tasked with undertaking a thorough investigation into the circumstances leading to the death of the Cheetah, examining all available evidence and coordinating closely with the Madhya Pradesh forest department to ensure strict and swift action in the matter.The 19-month-old radio-collared male cheetah, an offspring of Namibia-born Cheetah Nirva, was found injured on Oct 25 in the territorial forests of Morena, outside the protected area of Kuno National Park. Preliminary medical examinations corroborated multiple internal injuries associated with the firearm pellets.The incident, the first reported casualty of a shooting since PM Narendra Modi launched Project Cheetah at Kuno in Sept, 2022, is being viewed quite seriously at the Centre, given the critical importance of Project Cheetah and the need to ensure the highest standards of protection for the reintroduced population of the Big Cat.“As reported by the MP forest department, the injured cheetah was rescued from the Sheopur Territorial Forest Division the same day and provided intensive veterinary care and emergency surgery at the veterinary facility in Jabalpur. During the surgery, five firearm pellets were recovered from its body. Despite the medical intervention, the Cheetah succumbed to its injuries on Oct 27,” said the Union environment ministry in a statement.It said, “The state govt has already constituted a Special Task Force (STF), comprising forest and police officers, to investigate the incident. The central team deputed by the Union environment ministry would work in coordination with the state machinery. It would also examine the implementation of security protocols, as well as monitoring and protection measures being undertaken to avoid any such incident in future.“The central team would submit its findings and recommendations to the ministry for further directions to the state govt and field authorities.”The central team comprises the Inspector General of Forests, National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA), Additional Director, Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB), and Regional Deputy Director, WCCB.
Article Summary: 19-month-old radio-collared male cheetah, an offspring of Namibia-born Cheetah Nirva, was found injured on Oct 25 in the territorial forests of Morena, outside the protected area of Kuno National Park. Five firearm pellets were recovered from its body.

Article Title: UAE honours flydubai pilot Smit Machchhar who fought off co-pilot’s attack to save passengers
Article Text:
UAE honours Indian flydubai pilot for thwarting mid-air attack

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The UAE has honoured Captain Smit Machchhar and the crew of flydubai Flight FZ1073 for their courage in protecting passengers during a serious in-flight incident. UAE President Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan conferred the First-Class Order of Zayed II on the crew on Tuesday.The honour was presented by Dubai Crown Prince Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum.Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed, in the presence of UAE Vice President, Prime Minister and Dubai Ruler Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, also met the crew members on Tuesday.On September 30, Flight FZ1073, operating from Dubai to Tel Aviv, was diverted to Tabuk in Saudi Arabia following a serious incident in the cockpit. Captain Machchhar was injured, while crew members, off-duty pilots and passengers helped bring the situation under control. The aircraft landed safely, and all 172 passengers and crew were reported safe.During the meeting, the UAE leaders praised the crew for their courage and sense of responsibility in protecting passengers. They stressed that human safety and security remain the UAE's highest priority.While Machchhar was receiving treatment for his injuries, Sheikh Hamdan visited him and praised his courage, sense of responsibility and commitment to protecting human life.The deputy prime minister expressed pride in Machchhar being part of the "story of our nation"."During a visit to Captain Smit Machchhar… the flydubai pilot who embodied the highest degrees of courage, responsibility, and care for human life. From us, and from the leadership of the nation, he has our full appreciation and praise. We are proud that he is part of our team… part of the story of our nation… and part of what the UAE stands for… a nation of compassion… a nation of peace… and a nation of life," he wrote in a post on X.In an earlier interview with the UAE's state-owned newspaper The National, Machchhar recalled the attack by the co-pilot and said he suffered several blows before he could open the cockpit door.“The first time when I was hit … my thought was something's gone horribly wrong with the aircraft structure, which has fallen on my head. It almost made me fall on my control column. In the next couple of seconds, when the hits kept on coming, (I realised) it was the other person who I thought was supposed to be on the team.”“My immediate action was to free myself from the seat belts. And I tried to just block the blows as much as I could, because the blows were coming on the head… While the first few blows came in, my vision … it was so narrow. I lost a lot. I was just looking (at) outlines,” he told The National.“Immediately, my hand went to the knob which opens the door. And (I was) screaming for my colleagues. I believe that was the first time when I lost consciousness. I fell face down in the cockpit,” he added.Recalling the moment when the aircraft plunged 17,000 feet, Machchhar said, “The scariest thing that I heard and felt was the engines spooling down.”Despite the attack, Machchhar said his love for flying remained unchanged.“Did my love die for aviation? Not at all. Not at all. I'm just glad that I was able to do my part.”Machchhar managed to unlatch the cockpit door, allowing passengers and off-duty crew members to enter and restrain the co-pilot. The co-pilot had attacked him with an axe in an attempt to bring down the aircraft. A hijacking distress signal was also sent.The flight was diverted to Tabuk, where it made an emergency landing with the help of passengers who helped land the aircraft. All 180 occupants disembarked without injury, according to the account of the incident.Israeli President Isaac Herzog has also announced that he would confer Israel's Presidential Award for Civilian Heroism on Machchhar.
Article Summary: The UAE has honoured Captain Smit Machchhar and the crew of flydubai Flight FZ1073. UAE President Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan conferred the First- Class Order of Zayed II on the crew on Tuesday. The co-pilot had attacked him with an axe in an attempt to bring down the aircraft.

Article Title: NEET-PG counselling: Candidates struggle to join online as colleges remain unreachable
Article Text:
Candidates who have secured postgraduate medical seats through NEET-PG counselling 2026 are encountering challenges with the online joining procedure.

New Delhi: Candidates allotted postgraduate medical seats under NEET-PG counselling 2026 are facing difficulties completing the online joining process, with some reporting that nodal officers listed on the official portal are unreachable or their contact details are invalid.At Vardhman Mahavir Medical College (VMMC) and Safdarjung Hospital, candidates have complained that the nodal officer’s mobile phone is switched off and landline numbers are not reachable. The Medical Counselling Committee’s (MCC) helpline, they said, directed them to contact the allotted college, leaving them struggling to resolve admission-related queries.The problem is not limited to one institution. Candidates have also flagged similar difficulties with the University College of Medical Sciences (UCMS), where the portal displays a nodal officer’s mobile number as “00000000”, making it impossible to contact the designated official on that number. The portal lists an email address, but candidates have complained of not receiving a response.When contacted, a senior official told TOI, “we will take up the issue with the colleges and ask them to update their contact details so that students can reach the concerned officials during counselling. Incorrect or non-functional contact numbers create unnecessary difficulties for candidates. We will also raise the matter in a meeting and seek a resolution.”The issue assumes significance for candidates who have opted for the float option in counselling. Those choosingaccept the allotted seat, while candidates choosingwish to retain their current allotment while remaining eligible for an upgrade in subsequent rounds. Candidates who have to complete online reporting and submit documents are seeking timely verification and clear communication from their allotted institutes.The MCC portal itself displays a message stating that document verification is pending at the allotted institute and advises candidates to contact the nodal officer for admission-related queries. But when the listed contact details do not work, candidates are left without a clear channel to resolve their concerns.A social media post by a former J&K nodal officer for the Diplomate of National Board (DNB) programme also raised questions over outdated contact details. He said an MCC allotment letter dated October 23 listed his name and personal mobile number as the J&K nodal officer despite his having retired.Candidates say delays or confusion over document verification can leave them uncertain about whether their joining formalities have been completed within the prescribed timeline. They want the MCC and participating colleges to ensure that contact details are current, officials are reachable and admission-related queries are addressed promptly.The complaints raise questions about who is accountable for coordinating online joining during counselling, and what recourse candidates have when neither the college nor the helpline can resolve their queries.
Article Summary: Candidates who have secured postgraduate medical seats through NEET-PG counselling 2026 are encountering challenges with the online joining procedure. At Vardhman Mahavir Medical College and Safdarjung Hospital, candidates have complained that the nodal officer’s mobile phone is switched off and landline numbers are not reachable.

Article Title: Kharge remarks insult to PM’s office: Survey
Article Text:
File photoMallikarjun Kharge

NEW DELHI: A survey said Tuesday that a majority of respondents considered Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge ’s controversial remark against PM Narendra Modi as an “affront to the dignity of the PM’s office”.Most respondents also believed that it was a reflection of the main opposition party’s “desperation”, the survey conducted by Matrize News Communications said, adding 72% of the total 5,000 respondents held that Kharge’s remark demonstrated a “lack of respect for Sanatan culture and Indian values”.Kharge had sparked controversy Sunday with his “Modi ka baap bhi jayega” remark after a member of the audience interjected during his speech at a Patna event to say that “the PM would not go anywhere” . It said the survey was carried out between Oct 25 and 27 through CATI (Computer-Assisted Telephone Interviewing).

Article Title: Kashmiri Pandit activist arrested in cyberterrorism case
Article Text:
Representational image

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: Jammu and Kashmir police have arrested a Kashmiri Pandit activist, Rakesh Handoo, in a “cyberterrorism” case for allegedly manipulating and repeatedly circulating terror-related threat material.Handoo, who had unsuccessfully contested the 2008 Assembly elections against National Conference president Farooq Abdullah from Hazratbal constituency, was remanded in police custody for five days by a court in Sopore police district, north Kashmir, on Tuesday.On Sept 17, 2026, police in Baramulla had registered FIR No. 151/2026 against Handoo, resident of Faridabad, Haryana, on the complaint of a Kashmir migrant employee under the Prime Minister’s Rehabilitation Package.According to police officers, Handoo allegedly manipulated and repeatedly circulated terror-related threat material, purportedly issued by Soldier of Resistance, United Liberation Council, on X, falsely projecting the complainant as an intended target by altering the original material and superimposing the complainant’s name onto it.Handoo’s lawyer, Aazim Ahmad Pandit, said a bail application was initially moved before a magistrate after his client’s arrest as the defence was unaware of jurisdictional issues.He said they learned in court that police had invoked IT Act Secs 66F and 84C, with Sec 66F dealing with cyberterrorism, which comes under the National Investigation Agency (NIA) Act. “Once we realised that Section 66F had been invoked, we understood that the matter pertains to the designated court. We informed the magistrate that we would approach the competent court with a bail application,” Pandit said.The lawyer said his client was alleged to have shared certain information through an account on eight occasions. “Police have escalated the matter by invoking Sec 66F but the case doesn’t fulfil requirements of cyberterrorism offence,” Pandit said.Police officers said eight social media posts and relevant documentary evidence were seized from the accused, They said the accused had failed to join the investigation despite three notices, forcing police to obtain an arrest warrant.The accused, police offices said, was arrested on Oct 17, 2026, following due legal procedure, and two mobile phones were seized and X account details obtained for technical examination. They claimed offences under Sections 66F and 84C of the IT Act have been found prima facie established during investigation, while Forensic Science Laboratory and technical analyses reports were awaited.Threat letters to Kashmir Pandits had surfaced on social media in Aug this year. Police had tightened security in areas of the Valley where Kashmiri Pandits live and allowed some employees under the Prime Minister’s Package for Kashmiri Pandits to work from home temporarily. Kashmiri Pandit group Panun Kashmir had raised concerns over a purported threat letter from United Liberation Council, which named several Kashmiri Pandits and listed their phone numbers.
Article Summary: Jammu and Kashmir police have arrested a Kashmiri Pandit activist, Rakesh Handoo, in a ‘cyberterrorism’ case. Handoo was remanded in police custody for five days by a court in Sopore police district, north Kashmir, on Tuesday. He had unsuccessfully contested the 2008 Assembly elections.

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu minister Aadhav Arjuna launched a sharp attack on the DMK, claiming that the party had underestimated his side and was now in a weak position in the Maduranthakam constituency.Arjuna said the DMK had earlier claimed it would win 200 constituencies but was now sitting in the opposition benches.“The DMK, which said that it would win 200 constituencies, is sitting in the Opposition benches. They took us lightly. They said, ‘These people only know how to blow whistles.’ That very whistle came to us as our symbol, and we have blown them away completely with that whistle,” he said.Arjuna further claimed that the DMK was in a “pathetic position” in the constituency and questioned whether the party would even be able to retain its election deposit.“In this constituency, the DMK is in a pathetic position. Will the DMK even get its deposit back?” he said.He also targeted Tamil Nadu leader of opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin , alleging that his remarks were damaging the DMK.“Everything that comes out of the mouth of Udhayanidhi is only obscenity. No one else needs to come to destroy the DMK; MK Stalin’s son is enough. Udhayanidhi Stalin has come to destroy the DMK,” Arjuna said.Bypolls to the Maduranthakam Assembly constituency in Chengelpet district, adjoining Chennai, and the Dharapuram constituency in Tiruppur district of western Tamil Nadu will be held on October 6.The bypolls were necessitated after AIADMK legislators Maragatham Kumaravel and P Sathyabama resigned from their posts and joined the ruling TVK. The party has fielded both of them from the same constituencies they represented after being elected in the April Assembly election.This is the first time the TVK government is facing Assembly bypolls since it assumed office in May 2026.The Left parties, which extend outside support to the TVK government and help it retain its majority, have not joined the ruling party-led alliance. Instead, they are contesting the bypolls as a separate front.Candidates of the main opposition DMK, the AIADMK and the Tamil nationalist Naam Tamilar Katchi (NTK) are also in the fray.The Vanniyar-dominated PMK, which has considerable influence in several northern parts of the state, has not extended support to any party.A key opposition campaign plank is that the bypolls were not a natural outcome but were forced on voters after the TVK “lured AIADMK MLAs” to strengthen its numbers in the Assembly.AIADMK chief Edappadi K Palaniswami has already begun campaigning, seeking “justice” over what he has described as the betrayal.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu minister Aadhav Arjuna launched a sharp attack on the DMK. He claimed that the party had underestimated his side and was now in a weak position. Bypolls to the Maduranthakam Assembly constituency in Chengelpet district, adjoining Chennai, will be held on October 6.

Article Title: Why China Suspended La Liga Broadcasts After Kylian Mbappé's 'Dictator' Remark About Mao Zedong: Full Controversy Explained
Article Text:
Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe (AP/PTI)

What did Mbappé say about Mao Zedong?

Why has China suspended La Liga broadcasts?

Three Chinese brands end partnerships with Mbappé

A wider pattern of commercial fallout in China

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Kylian Mbappé has issued an apology after a video in which he appeared to describe China's founding leader Mao Zedong as a dictator triggered a backlash in China, costing the Real Madrid forward commercial partnerships and prompting Chinese state media to suspend broadcasts of Spanish football league matches featuring him.The controversy erupted after a clip of Mbappé discussing his favourite meme circulated on social media. His comments drew criticism from Chinese authorities, football officials and commercial partners, with demands for both the French footballer and his club, Real Madrid, to issue formal public apologies.In response, Mbappé acknowledged that his words had caused offence and expressed regret over the reaction in China.“My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world,” he said in a statement on Tuesday.“I apologize to everyone my words have upset. This was absolutely not my intention. I have deep respect for the Chinese people and their history, and I am sincerely sorry.”The controversy stems from a video in which Mbappé was asked to identify his favourite meme featuring himself.The French forward replied that it was “a video someone made of a guy ... I think he was a Chinese dictator”. The clip then showed an edited image placing Mbappé's face on the body of Mao Zedong, China's revolutionary leader and the founder of the People's Republic of China.Football fans on social media frequently use the term 'dictator' jokingly to describe Mbappé, who is often portrayed in memes as overshadowing his teammates and even the clubs he represents. Images depicting him as Mao and other authoritarian leaders have also circulated online.However, the reference to Mao proved particularly sensitive in China, where the former leader continues to be revered by many despite the controversial legacy of his rule.Mao led the Communist Party through its formative years and its victory over the Nationalist Party in the civil war, before establishing the People's Republic of China. His rule also included campaigns such as the Great Leap Forward, an industrialisation drive that contributed to a famine estimated to have killed around 30 million people.The combination of the dictator reference and the edited image prompted criticism in China, turning what appeared to be a joke about a football meme into a wider controversy.The fallout extended beyond Mbappé after Chinese authorities and state media demanded an apology from the player and Real Madrid.China Media Group announced that it had suspended broadcasts of matches in La Liga and other games featuring the French star. It also removed advertisements featuring him and called on Mbappé and Real Madrid to issue apologies.The China Football Association separately said it had “lodged a stern protest” with Real Madrid and demanded a “public and formal apology” from both the player and the club. It said it firmly opposed remarks that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people.The broadcast suspension puts La Liga's commercial relationship with China under pressure, given the country's importance as a market for the Spanish competition.La Liga responded by distancing itself from the comments, saying Mbappé had spoken in a personal capacity and did not represent the league.In a statement, it said it “deeply regrets the offense caused to Chinese fans by Mbappé's recent comments”.The league also announced plans to introduce a communication protocol for players and clubs, while working with stakeholders in China to prevent similar incidents in the future.La Liga president Javier Tebas later said on X that he had met China's ambassador to Spain, Yao Jing, to discuss the controversy and seek a resolution.Tebas reiterated the league's commitment to maintaining its partnerships with China, including its strategic agreement with the Chinese league through 2029 and its deals with China Media Group.“Our commitment is to keep working together so that an individual episode does not harm the important advances achieved nor affect the millions of Chinese fans who follow our competitions. China is and will continue to be a strategic partner for La Liga,” Tebas said.The backlash has also affected Mbappé's commercial interests in China, where his image has featured prominently in advertising campaigns, from subway stations to elevator displays.Beverage company Dongpeng, dairy giant Mengniu and cheese maker Milkground announced on Tuesday that they were ending their agreements with the footballer.The companies issued similarly worded statements opposing “any words and actions that hurt national sentiment”. Although they did not specify the precise reason for their decisions, their announcements followed the circulation of the video featuring Mbappé's comments about Mao.Mbappé has appeared in campaigns for products ranging from electrolyte drinks to milk and cheese. One Dongpeng advertisement featured him delivering a slogan in Chinese, while a Mengniu commercial showed him alongside Argentine football star Lionel Messi.Chinese social media platform RedNote also joined the criticism. It said its content partnership with Mbappé had ended on December 31, 2024, and announced that it would remove related promotional material. The platform expressed opposition to “any conduct that hurts national sentiment”.Mbappé's RedNote account was also banned from accepting new followers on Tuesday.On Weibo, hashtags relating to Dongpeng ending its partnership with the footballer and several brands cutting ties with him topped the trending list. Calls to boycott Mbappé also gained traction, with some users criticising his remarks and telling him not to visit China.The controversy is the latest example of the repercussions foreign public figures and organisations can face in China over remarks perceived as offensive to the country.In 2019, Chinese state television stopped broadcasting NBA games after Daryl Morey, then general manager of the Houston Rockets, tweeted in support of anti-government protesters in Hong Kong.The latest episode has similarly drawn in commercial partners, sports administrators and broadcasters, with La Liga attempting to contain the damage to its relationship with Chinese audiences.While Mbappé has apologised and the Spanish league has distanced itself from his comments, the incident has highlighted how a remark made in the context of an online football meme can escalate into a dispute with consequences for broadcasting and commercial partnerships.
Article Summary: Kylian Mbappé has issued an apology after a video in which he appeared to describe China's founding leader Mao Zedong as a dictator triggered a backlash in China. The controversy erupted after a clip of Mbappe discussing his favourite meme circulated on social media. His comments drew criticism from Chinese authorities, football officials and commercial partners, with demands for both the French footballer and his club, Real Madrid, to issue public apologies.

Article Title: 'The whole tide turned': Trump takes credit for Netanyahu's showing in Israel elections
Article Text:
Trump claims endorsement turned the tide for Netanyahu

US president Donald Trump has claimed that his endorsement helped Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu turn the tide in Israel’s 26th Knesset election, contributing to the incumbent’s better-than-expected performance. Partial results showed Netanyahu’s bloc leading the race but falling short of the majority needed to form a government.With 57.3% of ballot boxes counted as of 7:58 am, partial results released by the Central Elections Committee showed the pro-Netanyahu bloc securing 55 seats, against 49 for the anti-Netanyahu bloc. Arab parties were projected to win 16 seats.Meanwhile, Reservists, with 2.6% of the vote, People of Israel, with 1.7%, and Charedi Public, with 0.2%, remained below the 3.25% electoral threshold required to enter the Knesset. Votes cast in double envelopes, including those of soldiers, are counted later.On Wednesday, Trump took to Truth Social, where he shared comments by Irving C Schwartz, “When President Trump endorsed Bibi Netanyahu, the whole tide turned, and now, rather than a decisive defeat for a Great Prime Minister, it looks like a big come-from-behind stalemate, or even a WIN for Netanyahu."It all took place AFTER the Endorsement by President Trump, who only wants what is good for the Middle East, Israel, and the United States of America!”Additionally, The Jerusalem Post reported that, while speaking to reporters on the tarmac near Air Force One after attending a rally in Texas, Trump said the Israeli leader had exceeded expectations.“I heard the poll numbers were wrong..., the exit polls; I heard he [Netanyahu] did very well. It was pretty close, but very well. When the endorsement went out, it helped him a lot,” Trump said.He added, “It's a little bit early, but I'm hearing in Israel, top people say, 'Wow! He did a lot better than people thought.' It's looking like maybe a stalemate or a win.”The remarks came after Netanyahu publicly highlighted Trump’s support ahead of the election. In a televised appearance late on Sunday night, the Israeli prime minister praised the US president’s backing.“US President Donald Trump has come with a friendship that has never existed before between an Israeli prime minister and an American president. And it is doubtful we will ever have such a friendly president again,” Netanyahu said.“He has another two years, and he says he is calling on you to vote for me.”Trump had urged Israelis to back Netanyahu in a social media post on Sunday, writing: “Vote for Bibi Netanyahu for Prime Minister, we have to finish the job that we started!”Netanyahu also suggested that the two countries could take further action against Iran, saying Trump was willing to act “that would finally, finally, remove the Iranian threat”. He added that he had instructed Israel’s intelligence agency, Mossad, and the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) to pursue regime change in Iran.Meanwhile, the exit polls suggested that Netanyahu’s bloc and Eisenkot’s each won about 51 seats, and Arab parties won about 18. Netanyahu called for a right-wing government, claiming his bloc had a “significant, decisive majority” among Jewish voters and those supporting a Jewish state.
Article Summary: US president Donald Trump has claimed that his endorsement helped Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu turn the tide in Israel's 26th Knesset election. Partial results showed Netanyahu’s bloc leading the race but falling short of the majority needed to form a government. With 57.3% of ballot boxes counted, partial results showed the pro-Netanyahu bloc securing 55 seats, against 49 for the anti-Net Netanyahu bloc.

Article Title: We’d rather die than give up land: Siang villagers on proposed dam project
Article Text:
In Geku, John Panyang and fellow Adi farmers stand firm against the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project, fearing for their land and heritage. The situation escalates as security forces confiscate traditional daos from the villagers, igniting community anger. Ongoing protests disrupt agricultural activities, casting doubt on the imminent paddy harvest as the Adi community prioritizes their fight for their ancestral rights over farming needs.

GEKU: Every morning, John Panyang ties aaround his waist. The two-foot-long machete, carried in a bamboo or wooden sheath and slung across the shoulder, is an everyday companion for the Adi people of Arunachal Pradesh’s Siang region. Farmers use it to clear vegetation, cut bamboo and tend their fields. It is also woven into community life and identity — much like theis for Sikhs.But in villages at the centre of a growing resistance to the proposed 11,200 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP), it has become a source of tension.Security forces have reportedly seized the traditional implement from villagers in Riga and Pangkang, across Siang river from Geku, following an alleged attack on personnel with a. The seizures, carried out as part of heightened security measures against anti-dam protests, have stirred anger in the Adi community. Many Adi farmers openly defied the order to tend to their fields, especially in Geku — the nerve centre of protest against SUMP.The main reservoir of the proposed mega dam is reportedly planned near Geku village, about 35 km downstream from district headquarters Yingkiong.“We tie thearound our waist before stepping out of our homes every morning. It is an essential part of our lives. Why should we be stopped from carrying it to our fields?” said Panyang, a farmer living along Siang river in Geku town.Residents fear the govt’s security offensive is aimed at silencing opposition to the proposed dam and the pre-feasibility survey. Govt sources said NHPC wants to undertake drilling as part of the process of preparing the project’s pre-feasibility report. However, villagers have opposed any drilling in the riverbed, insisting that they do not want a feasibility report on the project.“We will not abandon our settlement. We would rather die here than surrender our land. If the Chinese dam is the threat, why should our govt build another mega dam in the Siang belt, nearly 300 km from the Line of Actual Control? The govt should explore alternatives closer to the border to counter China’s plans,” Panyang said.Twenty-seven villages across Upper Siang and Siang districts have joined hands to resist the project. The protests, however, have begun to affect the agricultural cycle, with several farmers unable to tend their paddy fields regularly because of demonstrations and meetings to plan further resistance.Along Siang river and its adjoining slopes in the narrow strips between hills, villagers cultivate traditional rice varieties such as ‘Gegong’, ‘Itanagar’, ‘Ngotsum’ and ‘Taker’. The latter is particularly significant among the Adis, who use it to prepare traditional rice beer.The agitation has also affected community festivities. On Sept 1, the Adi community in Geku curtailed its biggest festival, Solung, limiting celebrations to flag-hoisting at Gidii Notko, the traditional festival ground. The festival is usually celebrated over three to four days.For nearly 1,000 families in Geku, the proposed dam represents a threat to their homes, farmland and ancestral ties. Residents fear that construction upstream or downstream could expose the township to submergence risks arising from water storage or release.Most families in the remote settlement depend on agriculture, with only around 10 to 15 govt employees among its nearly 1,000 households. Many Adi families have lived on community land in the area for generations. In the 1960s, they moved from their original settlement at Kumku, situated on a hilltop about six kilometres away, to the riverbank to cultivate rice, oranges and vegetables.“We do not want compensation in exchange for losing our homeland. Where will we go, and what will we eat?” asked Oken Boli Panggyeng, a homemaker. “No dam survey, no detailed project report. That is our slogan,” she said, adding that villagers were prepared to prioritise the agitation over the upcoming paddy harvest.“Harvesting will begin in the first week of Nov. We may lose our paddy, but we do not want to lose our land. If the protests intensify, we may not go for the harvest at all,” she said.
Article Summary: The Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) is a proposed 11,200 MW dam in Arunachal Pradesh's Siang region. Security forces have reportedly seized traditional daos from villagers in Riga and Pangkang, across Siang river from Geku. The seizures have stirred anger in the Adi community.

Article Title: Israel election deadlock: Netanyahu, Eisenkot blocs tied in revised exit polls
Article Text:
File photo: Israel's prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Gadi Eisenkot

Opposition claims mandate for change

Arab parties could prove pivotal

Israel’s latest exit polls show a deadlock between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ’s bloc and the opposition led by Gadi Eisenkot, with updated projections from public broadcaster Kan and Channel 13 putting both sides at 51 seats each.Channel 12’s revised exit poll gives Netanyahu’s bloc 52 seats and the Eisenkot-led bloc 50, reversing its earlier projection that had the anti-Netanyahu camp marginally ahead.Turnout reached 77.7%, the highest recorded at the close of voting since 1999, according to Israel’s Central Elections Committee. The strong participation came in an election widely seen as a referendum on Netanyahu’s leadership after three years of war and regional conflict.Eisenkot arrived at Yashar party headquarters in Tel Aviv and said, “We made history,” arguing that the public had chosen change and voted against Netanyahu continuing as prime minister. He said it would be a mistake to hold another election given the high turnout and described respecting voters’ wishes as his responsibility.Opposition leader Yair Lapid also declared Netanyahu’s bloc had suffered a defeat. “Don’t let them confuse you: The Netanyahu bloc suffered a harsh defeat,” Lapid wrote on social media, adding that the public had told the government to go home.Netanyahu said it was too early to draw conclusions and that he was waiting for the “real results”. He maintained that Likud was the largest party and called for a “strong right-wing national government”, saying Israel could not be led by a government reliant on “Arab backing”.Kan projected 25 seats for Likud and 21 for Yashar, with the anti-Netanyahu bloc on 53 seats, Netanyahu’s bloc on 50 and Arab-led parties on 17. Channel 13 projected 25 seats for Likud and 23 for Yashar, with 53 seats for the anti-Netanyahu bloc, 50 for Netanyahu’s bloc and 17 for Arab-led parties. Channel 12’s revised projection put Likud on 24 seats and Yashar on 22, with the Jewish-led opposition parties on 52, Netanyahu-supporting parties on 50 and Arab-led parties on 18.The projected 17–18 seats for Arab-led parties could complicate coalition negotiations. Although they oppose Netanyahu, they are outside the main Zionist opposition bloc and have generally not joined governing coalitions. Their position could nevertheless become consequential if neither main bloc can secure enough support to govern.Neither main bloc is projected to reach the 61 seats required for a majority in the 120-member Knesset. The result could mean weeks of coalition negotiations and the possibility of another election. Netanyahu would remain caretaker prime minister in the interim, while President Isaac Herzog would consult party leaders and nominate a candidate to try to form a government.Official votes are still being counted, and exit-poll projections may change as further results come in.
Article Summary: Latest exit polls show a deadlock between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ’s bloc and the opposition led by Gadi Eisenkot. Neither main bloc is projected to reach the 61 seats required for a majority in the 120-member Knesset. The result could mean weeks of coalition negotiations and the possibility of another election.

Article Title: Attack outside Israeli embassy in Serbia: Cop kills knife-wielding attacker shouting 'Allahu Akbar'
Article Text:
In a shocking incident, a minor armed with a knife assaulted a security guard near the Israeli Embassy in Belgrade shortly after midnight. (Pic Credit: Reuters)

Attack follows political upheaval in Serbia and Israel

A knife-wielding assailant was shot dead after attacking a security guard outside the Israeli Embassy in Belgrade shortly after midnight on Wednesday, Serbian police said.Serbian interior minister Ivica Dacic said authorities were investigating the incident as a “terrorist attack”. The government raised the terror threat level to its highest category and increased security at key locations across the country, according to the news agency AP.According to Dacic, the attacker was a minor and was carrying two knives. He allegedly shouted “Allahu Akbar”, meaning “God is great” in Arabic, while attacking a member of Serbia’s Gendarmerie guarding the embassy.The officer sustained a minor facial injury but managed to shoot and kill the assailant in self-defence, the minister said.Photographs released by police showed the security booth outside the embassy, with the surrounding area cordoned off using police tape. Armed officers in tactical gear were seen at the scene.Dacic said the attacker was believed to have come from Sabac, a town in western Serbia. He added that security agencies had been monitoring the individual, whom he described as a supporter of the Islamic State group.“He kept the black flag in support of the Islamic State on his Instagram account,” Dacic said.The incident occurred days after Serbia held an early parliamentary election on Sunday, following nearly two years of protests against former president Aleksandar Vucic and his long-standing political leadership. A youth-led movement emerged as a major force in the election, although Vucic and his allies continue to control the police while the formation of a new government remains pending.Israel also held a parliamentary election on Tuesday, with exit polls indicating that no clear winner had emerged.The latest incident follows a similar attack outside the Israeli Embassy in Belgrade in June 2024. At the time, an assailant armed with a crossbow wounded a Serbian police officer guarding the diplomatic mission before being shot dead by a guard.
Article Summary: Knife-wielding assailant was shot dead after attacking a security guard outside the Israeli Embassy in Belgrade shortly after midnight on Wednesday. Attack follows political upheaval in Serbia and Israel. The government raised the terror threat level to its highest category and increased security at key locations.

Article Title: ‘Calculated, intentional act’: SIT says Gurgaon woman biker was deliberately rammed by car
Article Text:
Siya was travelling with her friends from Golf Course Road towards Extension Road when the accused, driving a white car, allegedly followed them and made obscene gestures.

(With inputs from PTI)





GURGAON: The Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing the road rage incident involving female biker Shivani Chauhan found that accused Kalyan Baisla deliberately rammed his car into her motorcycle after misbehaving with her.Police said all charges in the FIR, including attempt to murder, are likely to be retained in the chargesheet.The incident took place on September 13 and was captured on Shivani's helmet-mounted camera as well as a camera belonging to a fellow biker. It sparked outrage after she shared the video on social media.Shivani, alias Siya, a 27-year-old resident of Delhi's Kalkaji, was travelling with her friends from Golf Course Road towards Extension Road when the accused, driving a white car, allegedly followed them and made obscene gestures.His vehicle then rammed into her motorcycle from the side before fleeing the scene. The impact knocked her off the bike and sent her skidding on the road.After his arrest, Baisla admitted that the collision was his fault but denied hitting her deliberately, claiming he "lost control near a U-turn".However, the SIT concluded that "this was not an accident, but a calculated, intentional act", a senior police officer said.The investigation found that the accused car driver, Kalyan Baisla, had "deliberately rammed his vehicle into the female biker's motorcycle following an act of misbehaviour", the officer said.The five-member SIT, headed by ACP (Crimes Against Women) Sushila, recently submitted its report to the police commissioner."The SIT has prepared a draft of the charge sheet. The charge sheet will be filed in court within a week, in accordance with the sections of law applied in the FIR," ACP (Crimes Against Women) Sushila said.Following Shivani's complaint, Gurgaon police registered an FIR under Sections 78 (physical and digital stalking), 79 (use any word, sound, gesture, object, or intrusion of privacy with the intent to insult the modesty of a woman), 109 (attempt to murder) and 3(5) (common intention) of the BNS.The SIT was constituted by police commissioner Sibash Kaviraj following a notice from the Haryana Commission for Women.Four people were in the car at the time of the incident. Baisla and his cousin Lavnish were seated in the front.Gurgaon Police arrested Baisla and Lavnish in Rajasthan's Rajgarh, Dausa, on September 15. Both are currently lodged in Bhondsi Jail in Gurgaon after their bail pleas were rejected.
Article Summary: The incident took place on September 13 and was captured on Shivani's helmet- mounted camera as well as a camera belonging to a fellow biker. It sparked outrage after she shared the video on social media. The SIT concluded that "this was not an accident, but a calculated, intentional act"

Article Title: Myanmar national bound down for hosting 28 foreigners in Delhi without mandatory reporting
Article Text:
(AI image) Delhi Police has taken action against a Myanmar national for allegedly accommodating foreign nationals without proper documentation





NEW DELHI: Delhi Police has bound down a Myanmar national holding a UNHCR (Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees) card for allegedly accommodating 28 foreign nationals at a guest house in Uttam Nagar over a period of time without submitting mandatory details to authorities.According to police, the man allegedly hosted 23 US nationals and five Norwegian nationals at the premises but failed to file Form C (earlier referred to as Form III), which is required to be submitted by those providing accommodation to foreign nationals.The case was registered at Dabri police station on Oct 23 following a complaint from Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO).Police said the Myanmar national, who lives with his family in a four-room apartment in Chanakya Place, Uttam Nagar, allegedly used two rooms of the flat as a guest house and rented them out to foreign nationals over a period of time.The complaint, forwarded to DCP (Dwarka), alleged that the mandatory details of foreign guests were not submitted as required under immigration rules.FRRO termed the alleged lapse a violation of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025, and sought action under Sections 8 and 23 of the Act, Section 17 of the Immigration and Foreigners Rules, 2025, and relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).Following the complaint, Dabri police registered an FIR under Sections 8 and 23 of the Act and launched an investigation.Police said he has been bound down, requiring the Myanmar national to join the investigation whenever called and inform authorities before leaving the city.
Article Summary: Delhi Police bound down a Myanmar national for allegedly accommodating foreign nationals without proper documentation. The man allegedly hosted 23 US nationals and five Norwegian nationals at a guest house in Uttam Nagar. The case was registered at Dabri police station on Oct 23 following a complaint from Foreigners Regional Registration Office.

Article Title: Man travelling from Bengaluru to Shivamogga with family of 24 finds no water in train toilets, gets off at Tumakuru after station master fails to respond and spends extra Rs 1,760 on tickets for anoth
Article Text:
(AI image) A family of 24 traveling from Bengaluru to Shivamogga encountered severe toilet issues during their train journey

a





BENGALURU: A family of 24 travelling from Bengaluru to Shivamogga was forced to get off a train at Tumakuru after finding no water in the toilets and receiving no response from the station master. The family had to spend an additional Rs 1,760 on tickets for another train, prompting one of the passengers to approach the consumer commission.The Shivamogga District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has now directed South Western Railway (SWR) officials to refund the original ticket fare of Rs 1,000 with 6% annual interest and pay Rs 15,000 towards compensation and litigation expenses.Nagendra, a resident of PWD Quarters in Basavanagudi, Shivamogga, was travelling with 23 family members and relatives from Yesvantpur to Shivamogga on train No. 66575. The group had purchased general tickets worth Rs 1,000.When they discovered that the train's toilets had no water, they alerted the Tumakuru station master. However, after receiving no response, the family got off at Tumakuru and purchased tickets for another train, spending an additional Rs 1,760.Nagendra subsequently sent a legal notice to the railway authorities. After receiving no response, he filed a complaint before the consumer commission.On October 23, a bench comprising commission president T Shivanna and member BD Yoganand Bhandya directed the station masters of SWR, Bengaluru, and Tumakuru railway station to refund the original ticket fare of Rs 1,000, along with 6% annual interest calculated from April 15, 2025. The amount must be paid within 45 days, according to a release issued by the information department.The commission also ordered the railway authorities to pay Rs 10,000 as compensation for the inconvenience caused and Rs 5,000 towards litigation expenses within the same deadline.If the authorities fail to comply within 45 days, the amount will attract annual interest of 10% until full payment is made.
Article Summary: A family of 24 travelling from Bengaluru to Shivamogga was forced to get off a train at Tumakuru after finding no water in the toilets. The family had to spend an additional Rs 1,760 on tickets for another train, prompting one of the passengers to approach the consumer commission. South Western Railway (SWR) officials have been directed to refund the original ticket fare and pay Rs 15,000 towards compensation and litigation expenses.

Article Title: In 2013, British national Sarah Groves was found dead with 43 wounds on Kashmir houseboat; 13 years later court has ordered fresh psychiatric assessment of Dutch man accused of her murder
Article Text:
British national Sarah Groves (File Photo)





SRINAGAR: A team of doctors is set to re-examine Dutch citizen Richard de Wit, accused of murdering British national Sarah Groves in New Beauty houseboat in Dal Lake in 2013, at Srinagar’s Central Jail on Thursday to assess whether his psychiatric and general medical condition allows him to stand trial.“The present case has remained pending for a considerable period and the progress of the trial has from time to time been impeded due to the reported medical, particularly psychiatric, condition of the accused,” the court of the 2nd Additional Sessions Judge said.The court said that reports received from jail authorities disclosed that the accused has not been cooperating with psychiatric consultations, hospitalisation, medical examinations and the treatment advised by medical professionals.It was also reported that the accused had refused to cooperate with efforts to take him from the jail to an outside medical facility for examination and treatment.“The reported non-cooperation has, therefore, presented a practical impediment to securing the medical assessment necessary for determining the further course of the proceedings,” the court said. The court also said the question requiring consideration was whether, in view of his present psychiatric and general medical condition, the accused was capable of understanding the nature of the judicial proceedings, communicating meaningfully with his counsel and participating in the trial in accordance with law.Such a determination, it said, could not be made solely on the basis of a judicial impression or reports of non-cooperation, but required an objective and independent assessment by qualified medical professionals. The court then directed the Medical Superintendent, government psychiatric diseases hospital, Srinagar, to constitute a competent team of doctors for the fresh and comprehensive examination of the accused in the Central Jail, Srinagar, on October 29 2026.The court said the MS government psychiatric diseases hospital and the superintendent, central jail, Srinagar, should coordinate the necessary arrangements to ensure the presence of the medical team at the specified time. The court said the team should have a specialist in psychiatry, a specialist in general medicine, and specialist or medical practitioner as may be considered necessary in view of the reported condition of the accused,” the Court said, adding the examination within the jail should be conducted in an appropriate setting, with due regard to the dignity, safety and medical interests of the accused.On April 6, 2013, 24-year-old Sarah Groves was found dead inside her room in the New Beauty houseboat in Dal Lake in Srinagar. In the case of murder of Sarah Groves, the police arrested Richard de Wit, that time 43, around 77 kms, from the scene of murder, on the same day, a few hours after the murder. Richard De Wit, son of Handrik Pietor De Wit of Ridder Kerk Netherlands, according to the police chargesheet, was trying to move out from the valley, some hours after committing the murder. He was arrested in the town of Qazigund, around 70 km south of Srinagar. He was in wet clothes and without shoes. He was carrying his passport.Miss Groves had travelled to Srinagar in February that year as she was intending to stay in the valley for some time. De Wit arrived at the guesthouse on April 3, and was staying at the cabin next to Miss Groves. They were the only two tourists staying on the boat. De-Wit, according to the police, had allegedly stabbed Sarah to death. She had around 43 wounds on her body. Afadul Mujtaba, who was then Deputy Inspector General (DIG) police, Central Kashmir range, was first to question the accused had described him “having paranoia and had thought that the Dutch intelligence agencies were after him for his anti-government political beliefs and he had murdered Sarah presuming her as Dutch agent. ”
Article Summary: A team of doctors is set to re-examine Dutch citizen Richard de Wit. He is accused of murdering British national Sarah Groves in New Beauty houseboat in Dal Lake in 2013. The team will assess whether his psychiatric and general medical condition allows him to stand trial.

Article Title: Zeeshan Siddique, son of late Baba Siddique, appointed Mumbai NCP president
Article Text:
Zeeshan Siddique has been appointed the Mumbai divisional president of the Nationalist Congress Party.

Appointment letter

(With inputs from ANI)





MUMBAI: Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) president Sunetra Ajit Pawar on Wednesday appointed MLC Zeeshan Siddique, son of late Baba Siddique, as the party’s Mumbai divisional president.Siddique pledged to carry forward the legacy of his late father, Baba Siddique, and the vision of late party stalwart Ajit Pawar, outlining a roadmap to revive the party's urban base. He described his new role as both an emotional duty and a defining political responsibility.Speaking to ANI in Mumbai, Siddique thanked Sunetra Pawar and senior party leader Parth Pawar for placing their trust in him to lead the city unit, while recalling the legacy of his father and Ajit Pawar."It is a tremendous responsibility to be appointed as the Mumbai President of the Nationalist Congress Party. Sunetra Pawar Vahini Saheb and Parth Pawar dada, who is like an elder brother to me, have placed their faith in me. It is my duty to work for all sections and communities of society, connect youth and senior citizens, and expand the NCP family," Siddique said.Siddique also hinted at possible political realignments in Mumbai, claiming that several political workers, including many from the Congress, had been waiting for his formal appointment before joining the NCP."Many people from across parties, including several from the Congress, have been waiting to join our ranks once this responsibility was assigned.We will formulate a comprehensive roadmap to breathe new life into the Mumbai unit and ensure the NCP flag flutters across every corner of the city," he asserted."I remember my late father Baba Siddique ji today, as well as the vision that the late Ajit Pawar dada had for Mumbai. I will walk in their footsteps and work tirelessly to prove the leadership's trust right ahead of the upcoming elections," he added.Asked about the political controversy surrounding the delay in releasing the investigation report into the plane crash that killed Ajit Pawar, Siddique called for an impartial and comprehensive inquiry into the tragedy."Today marks exactly nine months since the passing of Ajit Pawar dada. Irrespective of what political spokespersons say, we all hold him as our mentor and guru. It is our collective demand that a comprehensive and fair investigation must be carried out to bring out the complete truth," Siddique said.On the Bombay high court granting interim relief to Bollywood actor Imran Khan by staying the 'Leave India' deportation notice until November 2, Siddique declined to comment on the specifics of the case."The matter is currently sub judice before the court, so I will not comment on the specifics. We have full faith in the judiciary and will respect whatever decision the court arrives at," Siddique said.
Article Summary: MLC Zeeshan Siddique has been appointed the Mumbai divisional president of the Nationalist Congress Party. Siddique pledged to carry forward the legacy of his late father, Baba Siddique, and the vision of late party stalwart Ajit Pawar.

Article Title: Cyclone Arnab: Landfall weakens to 'severe' cyclonic storm after crossing Andhra Pradesh-Yanam coast; 20,000 evacuated, trees uprooted, power cut in Konaseema, Kakinada
Article Text:
Electricity connections in parts of the state were expected to be restored by Wednesday evening, while major highways were expected to be cleared within hours.

VISAKHAPATNAM/KAKINADA/AMALAPURAM: Cyclone Arnab crossed the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts on Wednesday morning and weakened from a very severe cyclonic storm into a severe cyclonic storm, bringing heavy to extremely heavy rainfall, uprooting hundreds of trees and electric poles, disrupting power supply and communication, and damaging roads and standing crops across coastal districts.There were no reported casualties apart from a death due to electrocution in Visakhapatnam city. More than 20,000 people were evacuated from coastal districts before the cyclone made landfall.The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said the landfall process began around 1.20am on Wednesday and was completed by 9am, with the weather system moving entirely over land. Peak wind speeds reached 135 kmph, with gusts of up to 150 kmph.The cyclone crossed the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts southwest of Yanam, about 20km east-northeast of Narsapur, 40km southwest of Yanam and 60km southwest of Kakinada. Precautionary measures taken by the administration helped limit casualties in the state.Konaseema was among the worst-affected districts, with winds reaching up to 130 kmph. Trees and electric poles were uprooted, while standing paddy and horticulture crops were damaged.Roads were blocked, and power supply and communication were disrupted.Preliminary estimates indicated that hundreds of trees and around 100 electric poles had been uprooted in Kakinada district. No major damage was reported, and rainfall subsided after 2am on Wednesday. The Uppada coastal road in the district was completely washed away.In Visakhapatnam, hundreds of trees were uprooted and several low-lying areas experienced waterlogging. The city recorded more than 20cm of rainfall in 24 hours.Electricity connections in parts of the state were expected to be restored by Wednesday evening, while major highways were expected to be cleared within hours.Two National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams and two State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) teams had been deployed a day before the cyclone to undertake road clearance and rescue operations in response to emergency calls.In Alluri Sitharama Raju district, an old bridge at Tadiguda village in Anantagiri mandal was washed away. No injuries or casualties were reported in the incident.The IMD said the system was moving northwestwards and was centred about 20km east-northeast of Narsapur, 40km southwest of Yanam, 60km southwest of Kakinada, 90km east-northeast of Machilipatnam, 120km east of Gannavaram and 120km southwest of Tuni.It was very likely to move north-northwestwards over the next 48 hours and weaken gradually. The system was expected to weaken into a cyclonic storm within the next few hours and further into a deep depression over the subsequent six hours.The following rainfall figures were reported by the IMD:
