Article Title: Tamil Nadu environment minister blames household soaps for river foam; TTV Dhinakaran hits back
Article Text:
Tamil Nadu Environment and Climate Change Minister Dr V K Rajiv and AMMK General Secretary T T V Dhinakaran





CHENNAI: Tamil Nadu Environment and Climate Change Minister Dr V K Rajiv has sparked widespread debate after claiming that household wastewater, rather than industrial discharge, is responsible for foam in rivers.The controversy began during his visit to Tirupur, where he remarked that domestic soaps and shampoos were the primary causes of river frothing. Following heavy online backlash, the minister issued a clarification at the Chennai Secretariat. Defending his credentials, Rajiv said the chief minister had appointed him because of his medical background and emphasised his efforts to modernise the department. He asserted that recent statewide water studies had confirmed that industrial effluents were not to blame. Instead, he explained that domestic greywater containing high levels of phosphorus from soaps and shampoos naturally creates foam when it mixes with river water.Strongly condemning the minister’s remarks, AMMK general secretary T T V Dhinakaran slammed the government for deflecting responsibility onto ordinary citizens. In a post on X, Dhinakaran said attributing severe river pollution to everyday household soap use was absurd and reflected an alarming lack of accountability on the part of the Environment Department.Dhinakaran argued that shielding industrial offenders while ignoring systemic failures in waste management would only exacerbate environmental degradation. He demanded that the state government stop making bizarre excuses, strictly regulate industrial effluent discharge immediately, and implement robust sewage treatment infrastructure to protect Tamil Nadu’s vital river ecosystems.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu Environment and Climate Change Minister Dr V K Rajiv sparked widespread debate after claiming that household wastewater, rather than industrial discharge, is responsible for foam in rivers. AMMK general secretary T T V Dhinakaran slammed the government for deflecting responsibility onto ordinary citizens.

Article Title: Pune police write to Google & Apple to take down Rapido from their app stores
Article Text:
Pune police commissioner Amitesh Kumar confirmed that the police had sent a communication to tech firms

Pune:

TOI





City police, in their efforts to remove bike taxi option from Rapido’s app, reached out to Google and Apple.The move follows last week’s letter from Pune Collector and Regional Transport Authority chairperson Jitendra Dudi, asking police to shut down the bike taxi service.Pune police commissioner Amitesh Kumar confirmed that the police have written to Google and Apple. “We have already sent communications to Google Play Store and Apple’s App Store to put down Rapido’s application,” he toldPune RTO officials said the service could soon become unavailable unless Rapido secures the necessary approvals. The company’s application seeking approval to operate bike taxis has been pending with the transport department. “They were warned of legal action if they failed to comply with the norms. An FIR was lodged against them last week, and now the RTA chairperson and police have also stepped in,” an RTO official said, requesting anonymity.“If they comply with all requirements under the bike taxi policy, they may get approval. However, their unauthorised operations could complicate matters,” the official said.The bike taxi option remains active on the Rapido app and rides continue across the city despite an FIR being registered against it more than a week ago.Some commuters have questioned the authorities’ push to shut down the service, arguing that public transport remains inadequate and that passengers continue to face overcharging and misbehaviour by some autorickshaw and cab drivers.“I don’t understand why the authorities are so keen to close the service. They cannot ensure adequate public transport and do little when cabbies and autorickshaw drivers overcharge or misbehave. I used the [Rapido bike taxi] service a couple of days ago and found it perfectly fine,” said a Vimannagar resident on the condition of anonymity.Inder Rastogi, a young working professional and friend of the Vimannagar resident, said authorities should focus on regulating the service and improving safety rather than shutting it down. “One of the friends lives in Hinjewadi Phase III and has been watching empty Metro trains run for over a month. The govt has been waiting for the PM to inaugurate the service, with no clarity on when it would begin. Authorities could make bike taxis safer instead of trying to shut them down. The service operates successfully in several cities. They are buckling under pressure from autorickshaw unions,” he said.Autorickshaw unions, meanwhile, criticised the authorities for issuing letters without ensuring that operations cease. They also raised concerns about the verification of riders and passenger safety. “Only a few days ago, the Maharashtra Anti-Terrorism Squad caught a bike taxi operator who allegedly had links with a terrorist organisation in Pakistan. It is high time the service was stopped,” said Keshav Kshirsagar, president of Maharashtra Kamgar Sabha and Indian Gig Workers Front.
Article Summary: Pune police commissioner Amitesh Kumar confirmed that the police have written to Google and Apple. The bike taxi option remains active on the Rapido app and rides continue across the city despite an FIR being registered against it more than a week ago.

Article Title: 'Papa, mai maa ke pass ja rha hu': Jhansi teen records final video, shoots himself with father's pistol
Article Text:
In the Gursarai police station area of Jhansi, a 19-year-old BA student tragically died by suicide.

Video recovered from mobile phone

Father says son was under stress

Police investigation underway





JHANSI: A 19-year-old BA student allegedly died by suicide using his father’s licensed pistol at their home in the Gursarai police station area of Uttar Pradesh’s Jhansi district on Sunday morning.Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding his death after recovering a video he recorded on his mobile phone shortly before the incident.The deceased, Love Patel, was the only child of Munna Lal Patel, a retired village development officer who now works in agriculture.Love was found lying inside a room with a gunshot wound after neighbours alerted his family on hearing a gunshot. He was rushed to the Community Health Centre in Gursarai, where doctors declared him dead.Around 8am on Sunday, Munna Lal and his wife, Hemlata, left for the fields, leaving Love alone at home. Around two hours later, neighbours heard a gunshot and rushed to the house but found the door locked from inside.They alerted Munna Lal, who returned and found his son lying on the floor with a gunshot wound. His licensed pistol was found nearby.Police reached the spot and launched an investigation. A forensic team collected evidence, and the body was sent for a post-mortem examination.The video recorded by Love shortly before his death has become a key part of the investigation. In the recording, he reportedly addresses his father emotionally, saying he had caused him considerable distress and continued to trouble him.He then turns the camera towards a photograph of his mother and says, “Papa, paise apne paas rakho, ab mai maa ke paas ja raha hoon” (Dad, keep the money with you. I am going to be with my mother).He reportedly says he does not hold his friends, family members or relatives responsible for his decision.Police are examining the recording and other evidence to establish the circumstances surrounding his death. The reason remains unclear.During questioning, Munna Lal reportedly told police that Love often remained under stress and had difficulty sleeping at night. He said his son sometimes took medication to help him sleep. Police are examining these details, but no cause has been established.Love’s mother, Sangeeta Patel, died by suicide after setting herself on fire in 2009. Love had been living with his father since her death. According to the family, Munna Lal had married Hemlata before marrying Sangeeta, with whom he had Love.Garotha Circle Officer Piyush Kumar Pandey said Love was a resident of Singar village and was pursuing a BA degree.According to the officer, preliminary information indicates that Love locked himself inside a room and shot himself with his father’s licensed pistol. His family took him to the hospital, where doctors declared him dead.Police have questioned Munna Lal, while the forensic team has examined the scene and collected evidence. Investigators are also analysing the mobile phone recording and recording statements from family members to determine the circumstances leading to the incident.
Article Summary: Love Patel, 19, was the only child of Munna Lal Patel, a retired village development officer who now works in agriculture. His mother, Sangeeta Patel, died by suicide after setting herself on fire in 2009. Love was found lying inside a room with a gunshot wound after neighbours alerted his family.

Article Title: Woman’s hair catches fire during ‘Well Of Death’ bike stunt; video emerges
Article Text:
The woman biker subsequently loses her balance and falls to the lower section of the 20-foot-high structure.





JAMSHEDPUR: A woman stunt performer sustained burn injuries after her motorcycle caught fire while she was performing inside the ‘Well of Death’ at a fair held at the Durga Puja ground under Burmamines police station limits late evening on Sunday.According to police, the incident occurred when the 28-year-old woman was riding her motorcycle at high speed along the wooden walls of a cylindrical structure.A video of the incident has gone viral on social media.The video shows smoke and sparks suddenly emerging from near the motorcycle’s engine as the woman rides along the structure.Within moments, the motorcycle catches fire, with flames rapidly engulfing the vehicle. The video also shows the woman’s hair catching fire.She subsequently loses her balance and falls to the lower section of the 20-foot-high structure.At the time, three Maruti 800 cars were also performing stunts alongside the motorcycle, speeding along the wooden walls.The sudden blaze triggered panic among hundreds of spectators standing on the elevated platform, many of whom screamed and rushed to escape.Staff members of the Well of Death immediately rushed to douse the flames by pouring water and throwing soil on the burning motorcycle.Their prompt response helped prevent the fire from spreading to the dry wooden structure, averting a potentially major mishap. However, the motorcycle was completely gutted by the time the flames were brought under control.A fuel leak or technical malfunction is suspected to have triggered the fire, though the exact cause is yet to be ascertained.Burmamines police station officer-in-charge Kumar Sarayu Anand said the woman was safe and no casualties had been reported. He added that the permission granted for the fair at the Puja ground was valid until Sunday.Police are investigating the circumstances leading to the incident and whether the organisers had obtained the requisite fire department clearance to conduct the event.
Article Summary: A woman biker sustained burn injuries after her motorcycle caught fire. She was performing inside the ‘Well of Death’ at a fair held at the Durga Puja ground under Burmamines police station limits late evening on Sunday. A video of the incident has gone viral on social media.

Article Title: Kuno cheetah cub dies after suspected shooting outside protected area, first such case since 2022 reintroduction
Article Text:
A 19-month-old male cheetah cub found with gunshot wounds has died in Kuno National Park (File photo)





BHOPAL: A 19-month-old male cheetah cub at Kuno National Park, which was found with multiple pellets lodged in its abdomen after a suspected close-range shooting, has died, forest department sources said.The cub, one of Nirva’s offspring, had been shifted to a medical facility in Jabalpur for advanced treatment after being rescued from a forest area bordering Sheopur and Morena districts on the night of October 25.The death is a major setback for Project Cheetah and raises concerns over the safety of the big cats outside the protected park area.It would be the first reported suspected shooting of a cheetah since the species was reintroduced in India in September 2022.Three or four metal pellets had been detected inside the cub’s abdominal cavity. Investigators are examining the nature of the weapon used and the circumstances in which the animal was shot.The Special Tiger Strike Force (STSF), a specialised wildlife protection unit, has been deployed in the area. The forest department is also seeking assistance from the state police’s Special Task Force to identify those responsible, officials said.The cub was found injured by a monitoring team on the evening of October 25 while ranging in the territorial forest division of Morena, bordering Sheopur district.It was rescued overnight and brought to Kuno for initial medical examination before being shifted to Jabalpur for further treatment.Morena is known for its ravine-dotted terrain and the widespread availability of country-made firearms in some pockets.Investigators are exploring whether the animal was shot with a traditional bharmar, a muzzle-loading firearm, or a country-made 12-bore gun. A forensic and ballistic examination is expected to help establish the type of weapon used.Some officials suspect the shooter may have fired in panic after encountering the young cheetah in the forest, possibly mistaking it for a leopard.However, the motive and circumstances remain unconfirmed, and no suspect has been identified.In a statement, Kuno authorities said an investigation was under way to determine the cause of the injuries and that all possible angles were being examined.The statement, issued by the Additional Principal Chief Conservator of Forests and Field Director of the Cheetah Project, did not explicitly mention a shooting.State chief wildlife warden Samita Rajora had earlier said the case was being investigated from all angles and that it was too early to comment on the cause of the injuries.The incident has renewed concerns about the threats cheetahs face while moving beyond protected areas. The first action plan for Project Cheetah had flagged the prevalence of bushmeat consumption and the possession of country-made firearms, bows, arrows and other hunting tools in the region.Poaching has been a persistent concern in the landscape around Kuno. In April 2022, months before the first cheetahs arrived from Namibia, a leopard was killed by poachers in the park’s buffer zone.Deer poaching has also been reported in surrounding areas, while forest officials have previously suspected hunting groups of entering protected areas and removing camera traps to avoid detection.Cheetahs were declared extinct in India in 1952. Their return is the centrepiece of Project Cheetah, launched in 2022, under which animals were brought from Africa to Kuno as part of a programme to re-establish the species in the country.Wildlife activist Ajay Dubey has demanded a CBI inquiry into the matter following interstate ramification.
Article Summary: 19-month-old male cheetah cub found with gunshot wounds has died in Kuno National Park. Three or four metal pellets had been detected inside the cub’s abdominal cavity. Investigators are examining the nature of the weapon used and the circumstances in which the animal was shot.

Article Title: IISER Pune removes Umar Khalid's book from library ‘to avoid unrest’
Article Text:
The controversy divided opinion online, with a section criticising a central science institute for recommending the book, while another defended it as a researched work on Adivasis.





PUNE: Indian Institute of Science Education and Research (IISER) Pune has withdrawn ‘Fractured Communities’, a book based on the PhD thesis of jailed activist and former JNU researcher Umar Khalid, after its inclusion in the Srinivasa Ramanujan Library triggered a social media controversy over the weekend.The institute said the book was retracted “as a precaution in order to avoid any misunderstanding or unrest” after the matter was brought to the authorities’ attention. “The book collection at the institute library is built through recommendations from institute members, and a dedicated committee oversees the functioning of the library. On average, over 50 books from various areas are routinely added every month to the library,” the institute said in a statement.“Regarding the book in question, as soon as the matter was brought to the attention of institute authorities, it has been decided to retract the book as a precaution in order to avoid any misunderstanding or unrest. The institute will examine what further action or steps can be taken,” the statement read.The controversy began after a photograph of the book displayed on the library’s digital board under the title ‘New Additions of Books’ was shared on ‘X’ by the handle @GemsofAcademia on Saturday night.The post was widely shared, with Madabhushi Madan Gopal, chairperson of the institute’s board of governors, responding through his personal ‘X’ account.“As in-charge chairperson, BoG, IISER Pune, I am shocked to know this. This is retracted last night and action is initiated on those who played this mischief. I assure such things will not happen again in IISER Pune. Prof. Sunil Bhagwat, Director, has taken immediate steps. We need to be alert,” he wrote.In a subsequent post, Gopal said the institute had identified the person responsible for this and that prompt action had been initiated. “There should be suitable remedial measures,” he posted.Asked about the action referred to in Gopal’s posts, an IISER Pune official said the chairperson had tweeted in his personal capacity through his personal account.The controversy divided opinion online, with a section criticising a central science institute for recommending the book, while another defended it as a researched work on Adivasis.‘Fractured Communities: Adivasi Histories and the Politics of Power’, released earlier this year, examines the history of Singhbhum’s tribal societies and is based on Khalid’s PhD thesis at Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU). Khalid has been lodged in Delhi’s Tihar Jail since 2020 as an undertrial prisoner in connection with a case registered under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) and other provisions of law. He was recently named the Asia-Pacific recipient of the Front Line Defenders Award for Human Rights Defenders at Risk.
Article Summary: Indian Institute of Science Education and Research (IISER) Pune has withdrawn ‘Fractured Communities’ The book is based on the PhD thesis of jailed activist and former JNU researcher Umar Khalid. The controversy divided opinion online, with a section criticising a central science institute for recommending the book.

Article Title: Road rage: 3 held for dragging Bengaluru cook to death under car
Article Text:
Three individuals were arrested in connection with the death of 25-year-old Ranjit Kumar Sahu





BENGALURU: Police have taken three people into custody after a 25-year-old cook was fatally dragged beneath a car for nearly 150 metres in a road rage incident at Electronics City.However, the owner of the car, who was with the other accused at the time of the incident, is at large.The accused are Ajay Rabidas, 26, Sajal Namasudra, 19, and Bijon Ray, 27, all residents of Basapur.The men from Assam work as drivers for cabs and trucks. The car owner, Shyam Khoar, also from Assam, is yet to be traced. Police investigations revealed that Rabidas drove the car, mowing the victim. All the accused claimed before the cops that they were heavily intoxicated following a party.The victim, identified as Ranjit Kumar Sahu, worked as a cook at a paying guest (PG) accommodation in BTM Layout. He had travelled to Electronics City to celebrate Dussehra with his friends.According to a complaint filed by Sahu’s friend, Nitish Kumar Mukhiya, the incident unfolded around 1.50am on Oct 21.Mukhiya and a group of friends were crossing the main road near Pragathipura, close to Electronics City, when a white car driven at high speed narrowly missed hitting them.Mukhiya waved his hand and used sign language to signal the driver to slow down and query the reckless driving. Taking offence at the gesture, the driver stopped the vehicle down the road, made an abrupt U-turn, and returned to the spot.Four men alighted from the car, leading to a heated altercation.Sensing trouble, Mukhiya phoned Sahu, who was resting at Mukhiya’s residence about 400 metres away. As Sahu reached the spot, the confrontation escalated into a physical clash.The car occupants decided to flee and started the engine. Sahu was standing directly in front of the vehicle. Despite seeing him, the driver accelerated the car. Sahu became trapped beneath the front portion of the car and was dragged along the road for approximately 150 metres, the complaint said.The vehicle eventually came to a halt. The occupants stepped out, pulled the severely injured Sahu from under the car, dumped him near the service road, and fled the scene. Sahu, who suffered critical injuries, was rushed to a private hospital at Madiwala, where he succumbed to his injuries.Deputy commissioner of police (Electronics City) M Narayana said, “CCTV footage we collected from the place of incident did not clearly show the car in detail. We interacted with local residents, in particular those who run all-night eateries on pavements; these interactions helped in identifying the vehicle and reaching the suspects. Finally, technical assistance also helped in solving the case.”
Article Summary: Ajay Rabidas, 26, Sajal Namasudra, 19, and Bijon Ray, 27, all residents of Basapur, have been arrested. The car owner, Shyam Khoar, also from Assam, is yet to be traced. All the accused claimed before the cops that they were heavily intoxicated following a party.

Article Title: 2 weeks, 2 Keralam teen drivers, 2 luxury cars, 4 deaths: How parents can be held liable when minors take the wheel
Article Text:
Controversies continue to erupt as Kochi witnesses cases of reckless driving, including a crash involving a Mini Cooper (L) and a Mercedes (R)





KOCHI: In two weeks, two reckless teen drivers pushed four families into grief.The two cases put not only the accused but also their parents in the dock, legally and morally.Legal experts said parents, who allow their children to drive, can’t claim ignorance of a minor taking a vehicle to evade legal repercussions.Under Motor Vehicles Act , the burden is on the parents to prove what precautions they took to prevent it, they said.Retired HC judge B Kemal Pasha said the father of the teenager who rammed a luxury sedan and killed a 55-year-old scooter rider cannot defend himself by claiming that his son had taken the vehicle without his knowledge.The fact that the teen clocked over 100km/hr indicates that he had probably driven before, which can strengthen the father’s culpability, said Pasha.“If he is driving above 100, then it is not his first time. He must have practised and I don’t think this was an isolated incident and he (dad) cannot say that he was unaware,” said Pasha, adding that it is surprising that the father is a judge, who is aware of the law.Since the father is the registered owner, it was his responsibility to keep the car keys safe.Even if he says that his son took the vehicle without his knowledge, it would mean he created the circumstances for him to do so.MV Act clearly places the burden on the vehicle owner or guardian to prove that the offence was committed without his knowledge or that he had exercised due diligence to prevent it.That means he needs to prove that it was done without his knowledge. It is not easy, said Pasha.He said the action taken in the case should send a strong message to parents about allowing minors to drive.The accident at Nedumbassery also had an element of parental involvement. After the accident, the accused teen reportedly told people that his father would take care of the case.Senior consultant psychiatrist at Medical Trust Hospital Dr CJ John said boys have a fascination for vehicles.“They instinctively want to drive if there is a vehicle at home. There is a section of parents who succumb to their demands or even boast about it before others instead of firmly telling their children that it is illegal. By doing so, parents plant the seeds of indiscipline and lawlessness at a young age,” he said.John added that when such parenting combines with teenagers’ risk-taking and rebellious behaviour, children may feel that such conduct has been sanctioned. He said the issue also reflects the lack of proper law enforcement.
Article Summary: In two weeks, two reckless teen drivers pushed four families into grief. The two cases put not only the accused but also their parents in the dock, legally and morally. Legal experts said parents, who allow their children to drive, can’t claim ignorance of a minor taking a vehicle.

Article Title: How dispute over hotel lease escalated into mass shooting at Guwahati's Bilas Inn, with leaseholder killing 4 linked to owner's family
Article Text:
A deadly shooting occurred at Hotel Bilas Inn in Guwahati, leaving five people dead and one injured.

Accused arrested, licensed pistol seized

Congress raises law and order concerns

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think is the most important step to prevent such incidents? Stronger law enforcement Faster resolution of property disputes Stricter firearm regulations Better conflict resolution mechanisms 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





GUWAHATI: A dispute over a hotel lease allegedly escalated into a deadly shooting in Guwahati on Monday night, leaving five people dead and another injured.The victims included the hotel's co-owner, her son and daughter-in-law, her brother and the property’s caretaker.The accused, identified as Ghanakanta Gogoi, the hotel's leaseholder, was arrested within an hour of the incident, police said.Gogoi allegedly opened fire at Hotel Bilas Inn on GS Road, opposite Bora Service, around 9pm. The hotel is about 2km from the Assam Police headquarters.The victims were associated with the hotel's ownership and management. Four of the deceased belonged to the same family, while the fifth person was from their village, Guwahati police commissioner Partha Sarathi Mahanta said. The injured survivor was also from the same village.“Preliminary investigation suggests that the incident stemmed from a property dispute related to the lease agreement of the hotel,” Mahanta told reporters outside the property.Gogoi had taken the hotel on lease about a year ago, the commissioner said, adding that investigators were examining all aspects of the incident to establish the sequence of events.Police apprehended Gogoi in the Paltan Bazar area within an hour of the shooting.A licensed .32-bore pistol, suspected to have been used in the killings, was seized from him.“Six persons sustained gunshot wounds, of whom five succumbed to the injuries. One person is undergoing treatment,” Mahanta said.Three of the deceased have been identified as Helena Bharali, Deborshi Kashyap and Narayan Das, while the identities of the remaining victims were being verified.The sole survivor, identified as Satyen Pathak, 42, sustained a bullet injury to his shoulder and was undergoing treatment at Gauhati Medical College and Hospital. His condition was stable, a senior doctor said.A forensic and scientific investigation is underway, with specialised teams examining the crime scene and collecting evidence. Police said further investigation would establish the precise circumstances that led to the shooting.Assam Congress president and Jorhat MP Gaurav Gogoi expressed grief over the killings and raised concerns about public safety in Guwahati.In a social media post, Gogoi offered condolences to the victims' families and said the incident raised serious questions about the city's law and order situation. He called on chief minister and home minister Himanta Biswa Sarma to take responsibility and pay greater attention to rising crime.Gogoi, the deputy leader of the opposition in the Lok Sabha, also called for a thorough inquiry, accountability and concrete measures to prevent similar incidents.
Article Summary: A dispute over a hotel lease allegedly escalated into a deadly shooting in Guwahati on Monday night. The victims included the hotel's co-owner, her son and daughter-in-law, her brother and the property’s caretaker. The accused, identified as Ghanakanta Gogoi, was arrested within an hour of the incident.

Article Text:

AMRITSAR: The son of an Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) sarpanch was shot dead and his friend was injured when assailants opened fire on them outside a gurdwara in Cheete Kalan village, falling under Chatiwind police station, on Monday evening.The victim, Teerath Singh, was returning after paying obeisance at the gurdwara along with his friend Ranjit Singh when the assailants allegedly opened indiscriminate fire, leaving both injured.Teerath was rushed to a hospital, where doctors declared him brought dead, officials said.Yadwinder Singh, Deputy superintendent of police (DSP), Attari, said that Ranjit, who sustained a bullet injury, is undergoing treatment and is stated to be out of danger.The preliminary investigations suggested that the murder stemmed from an old animosity over a land dispute, the DSP said while ruling out any political rivalry.He further said police have identified four persons, Gurditt Singh, Gurjant Singh, Harkirat Singh alias Hockey, and Gora, and registered an FIR naming them, but no arrests have been made so far.The DSP said that teams have been constituted to investigate the case and arrest the accused.Police sources also informed that the family of Teerath also suspects the involvement of a rival group from the village behind the incident.Notably, Teerath’s brother Karaj Singh had won the sarpanch election on an AAP ticket.The killing triggered a political attack on the AAP government, with former union minister Ravneet Singh Bittu questioning its ability to maintain law and order in Punjab.In a X post, he said, “The murder of Teerath Singh, brother of an incumbent AAP sarpanch, outside a gurdwara in Amritsar is a stark indictment of Punjab’s collapsed law and order. Not a single day passes without the state being shaken by gunfire. When even the ruling party’s own representatives and their families are not safe, the security of ordinary citizens is left in God’s hands. Bhagwant Mann must be held accountable for this spiralling violence. ""Either enforce the writ of the state and ensure people’s safety, or resign. Punjab cannot be expected to keep picking up bodies day after day,” the post read further.
Article Summary: Teerath Singh was shot dead outside a gurdwara in Cheete Kalan village. His friend Ranjit Singh sustained a bullet injury. Preliminary investigations suggest that the murder stemmed from an old animosity over a land dispute, the DSP said while ruling out any political rivalry.

Article Title: At least 30 killed as high-speed train rams another in Spain's Toledo; videos show gutted carriages
Article Text:
The scene of a collision between two trains in Spain's Urda (Credit: AP)

Part of a wrecked train is photographed at the site of a train collision in Spain (AP photo)

At least 30 people were killed after two high-speed trains collided in Spain's central province of Toledo on Wednesday morning, reported Spanish local media.Several passengers are feared to have been injured in the crash, which has disrupted rail services connecting Madrid with Ciudad Real and Andalusia. The toll is likely to climb up as several people are critically injured.Spain's rail infrastructure operator ADIF confirmed the accident and announced the suspension of services on the affected routes.According to Spanish state broadcaster TVE, the collision involved two high-speed trains travelling in the same direction. One train reportedly struck the rear of the other, causing two carriages to come off the tracks.Expressing shock over what he called a "serious train accident", Spanish PM Pedro Sánchez said: "Emergency services are working on the ground to assist those affected and ensure their safety, in coordination with all the involved administrations. My affection, solidarity, and support to all the victims and their families."Manuel Galán, the mayor of the nearby town of Urda, told TVE that passengers had been injured.Civil protection officials had asked the town council to prepare a sports pavilion to receive passengers affected by the crash.Jesús Pérez, mayor of the neighbouring village of Los Yébenes, also said the incident appeared to be "serious.”Emiliano García-Page, president of the Castilla-La Mancha region, said in a post on X that he was travelling to the crash site.The accident comes months after another deadly train crash shook confidence in Spain's rail network. In January, 45 people died in southern Spain when a train derailed and collided with an oncoming train. It was the country's deadliest rail disaster since a 2013 crash that killed 80 people, raising fresh concerns about the safety of Spain's extensive high-speed rail system.
Article Summary: Two high-speed trains collided in Spain's central province of Toledo. Several passengers are feared to have been injured in the crash. The toll is likely to climb up as several people are critically injured. One train reportedly struck the rear of the other, causing carriages to come off the tracks.

Article Title: Worship before work: Just to make it out unharmed
Article Text:
Employees at Kidwai Bhawan express concern over the building's safety as they encounter daily hazards.





NEW DELHI: Every morning, about 150 employees walk into Kidwai Bhawan on Janpath, hoping to make it through another day without being injured. Staffers say as they enter the deteriorating building, they pray that no ceiling gives way, no chunk of concrete falls on someone’s head and no part of the ageing structure collapses while they are at work.Walking out unharmed at the end of the day brings relief, but the apprehension returns the next morning.Located opposite Janpath market, Kidwai Bhawan houses employees of Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Limited (MTNL) and Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited BSNL ). The building, which comprises two adjoining structures of eight and six floors, has extensive visible signs of deterioration -- cracked and peeling concrete, exposed reinforcement bars, damaged balconies, broken windowpanes and vegetation growing out of cracks are visible on its exterior. In several places, plaster has come off walls and ceilings, exposing brickwork and the material beneath the surface.Employees said the condition of the building has become increasingly alarming, with debris falling several times. In Aug, debris fell from the roof, injuring a woman. Instead of being moved out of the building, she was shifted to another room on the same floor, according to employees, who did not wish to be named.Workers alleged such incidents have become a recurring concern. “Whenever a portion of the building becomes unsafe after debris falls or structural damage is noticed, we are shifted to another room or floor, while work continues in other sections,” an employee claimed.According to some employees, about two years ago, a large structure near the rear parking had collapsed, following which signboards were placed warning people to stay away from areas where debris poses a safety risk. Workers said the warnings reflect the risks they face daily, but have not resolved the larger problem.The damage is not limited to the building’s exterior. Several employees flagged deteriorating ceilings, damaged walls and water accumulation inside, including in areas around washrooms. The condition of overhead sections has left workers worried that loose plaster or concrete could fall without warning. The balconies and exterior slabs have also raised concerns, with some portions appearing heavily weathered and damaged.The deteriorating condition has also affected routine maintenance. Employees TOI spoke to said technicians have refused to stand near certain balconies or work on air-conditioning units because the surrounding structure appears unsafe.According to staff, complaints have been made repeatedly to the authorities, but comprehensive repairs or a permanent solution have yet to materialise. Some also alleged that employees have been discouraged from raising the issue, but these claims could not be independently verified.For the employees, the concern is immediate and personal. They are not merely worried about inconvenience caused by shifting rooms, but that a more serious structural failure could put several people at risk at once.The building falls within the NDMC area but does not belong to the council. When contacted, NDMC chairman Manoj Kumar Dwivedi said the issue had never been brought to the council’s notice. “The matter will be looked into. A team will be sent to inspect the building and contact the building owners, MTNL and BSNL, to discuss the concerns raised, including the risks posed by falling concrete. Necessary action will be taken after the discussions with the owners,” he added. TOI's effort to get a reaction from the building owners didn't bear fruit.
Article Summary: Kidwai Bhawan houses employees ofMTNL and Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited BSNL. The building has extensive visible signs of deterioration -- cracked and peeling concrete, exposed reinforcement bars, damaged balconies, broken windowpanes and vegetation growing out of cracks.

Article Title: HC refuses to suspend sentence of juvenile killer
Article Text: New Delhi: Delhi High Court Tuesday declined to suspend the life sentence of a juvenile convicted of murdering an accused in custody outside Rohini Court in 2017.At the time of the attack near the court premises, he was a minor aged more than 17 years, according to the plea seeking relief. He was apprehended from the spot and was sentenced this Jan.According to Delhi Police, the convict was associated with the Neeraj Bawana Gang and carried out the murder of Rajesh Durmuth, a member of a rival gang, when the latter was brought by Haryana Police for a hearing.A bench of Justices Prathiba M Singh and Dinesh Bhatt refused to suspend the sentence after hearing arguments by the counsel for the appellant. The court took into account the fact that he had fired outside a court complex and shot dead a person who was in police custody.The defence counsel had submitted that the convict was in custody for seven years and nine months. It was also submitted that there were lapses in the investigation.The prosecution had highlighted that the convict was a serial offender, who was also named in other cases involving the Neeraj Bawana gang. Police said he was also booked in another case in Haryana’s Jhajjar, while he was on interim bail in the current case, which showed he was inclined to misuse his freedom.The prosecution also submitted that the appellant was convicted of the offences of firing and shooting a prisoner who was in police custody, an aggravating factor.The high court has listed the appeal against the conviction and sentence for hearing in Jan.
Article Summary: Delhi High Court declines to suspend the life sentence of a juvenile convicted of murdering an accused in custody outside Rohini Court in 2017. At the time of the attack near the court premises, he was a minor aged more than 17 years, according to the plea seeking relief.

Article Title: China 40-50km inside Arunachal, says state Congress chief Bosiram Siram
Article Text:

Thorough probe must be conducted: Siram

GUWAHATI: Arunachal Pradesh Congress president and former education minister Bosiram Siram on Monday alleged that Chinese troops have intruded 40 to 50 km deep into Indian territory in Upper Subansiri district.However, denying the claim, CM Pema Khandu said he did not believe any incursion was taking place.Siram said a Congress delegation led by him visited border areas from Aug 26 to 29, travelling from Itanagar via Nacho to Limeking and Taksing, and spoke with local residents. The delegation included Congress working president and former home minister Tanga Byaling and Upper Subansiri MP Jarodum Kri.The Chinese PLA have already advanced 40 to 50 km into Indian territory. Today, Chinese PLA personnel are stationed up there, at intervals. You can see the Army. They are on top of the mountains, while we are down below," Siram said.In June, a local group, Nah Welfare Society, first raised the flag saying the PLA had expanded its presence near Taksing, a claim that the Indian Army said was "incorrect and without any basis". In Aug, a People's Party of Arunachal team claimed that Indian patrols were being denied access to key points.Union minister Kiren Rijiju rejected a 60-km intrusion claim, but acknowledged increased Chinese activity on the high ridges.Responding to govt's denials, Siram asked, "If no intrusion or aggressive activity has occurred on the border, why are residents repeatedly raising these complaints? Instead of brushing off these allegations merely as rumours, a thorough and impartial factual investigation must be conducted."Siram also cited recent remarks by ITBP Director General Shatrujit Singh Kapoor on face-off locations, and said the ground reality reported by locals warrants a transparent, high-level probe by the Centre and the defence ministry."Serious border-related issues should not be ignored by dismissing them as allegations or rumours. The facts must be established to ensure the security of the country's borders and protect the rights and livelihoods of people living in border areas," he said."Entire areas have reportedly disappeared from the online maps and have come under its control. The whole of Asaphila has come under its control. And the strategically important areas, including the high ground, have already been taken over by China. They are under Chinese occupation."We are seriously concerned about the Chinese incursions and the situation along the India-China border. During our visit to the border areas, we found that the situation needs to be examined carefully," Siram added.He alleged that aggressive activity by the Chinese PLA has disrupted lives and traditional livelihoods of locals."The central govt and the ministry of defence must take immediate steps to ensure border security and protect the rights, livelihoods and traditionally used areas of residents....," he said.
Article Summary: Arunachal Pradesh Congress president and former education minister Bosiram Siram alleged that Chinese troops have intruded 40 to 50 km deep into Indian territory in Upper Subansiri district. Union minister Kiren Rijiju rejected a 60-km intrusion claim, but acknowledged increased Chinese activity on the high ridges.

Article Title: Mumbai locals hit by double disruption: 3 killed on tracks, 80 services cancelled, delays up to 90 minutes
Article Text:
Central Railway services were severely disrupted on a Monday due to a fire at a signalling hut (Photo credit: Imtiyaz Shaikh)





MUMBAI: Three people died in separate incidents on Central Railway tracks on Monday as services went haywire following a signalling hut fire and another disruption, forcing the cancellation of 80 local trains and delaying services by 70-90 minutes.The disruption affected thousands of commuters, stranded passengers in stationary trains for up to 90 minutes and also hit long-distance train operations.Thousands of commuters were stranded in stationary trains for up to 90 minutes, while some walked along the tracks as services operated intermittently on adjoining lines.A 21-year-old Mulund resident, Sahil Thite, died after being hit by a local train while crossing the tracks at Bhandup station. Two people were found dead on tracks between Ghatkopar and Vikhroli stations Monday evening.Police were yet to confirm the cause of their deaths.The CR disruption hit internal semester exams at a few colleges. As students struggled to reach on time, colleges rescheduled the exams.Commuters scrambled to find alternatives to reach their destinations by autorickshaws, buses and Metro on the first day of the week.“A signalling failure occurred at 9.33am after a fire broke out in the signalling hut at Kanjurmarg. Around 24 signals went blank across all six lines between Vikhroli and Bhandup,” said CR’s chief public relations officer Swapnil Nila.This came after a wire of unknown origin was found hanging from the overhead equipment on the Down slow line between Mulund and Thane at 9.23am.The breakdown affected both Main and Harbour lines. The latter also faced a shortage of train crews because personnel and resources were caught up in Main line operations.First, railway officials imposed a power block at 10am following the wire snag and restored the section at 10.48am. But by then, delays had already begun accumulating on the Main Line.Then, as signalling was unavailable following a fire, railway personnel introduced alternative operating procedures, including A-board authority and absolute block working on affected sections.Trains were allowed to proceed only after the prescribed safety clearances, reducing the frequency of movements and causing delays to accumulate across the network.The impact extended beyond suburban services, with both arrivals and departures of long-distance trains delayed as operational restrictions and cascading delays affected train movements, leading to packed platforms across stations.While all the signals were restored by 7.35pm, services continued to be delayed till late night.“An inquiry will be conducted to identify the cause of fire,” said Nila.Kurla GRP has registered a case of accidental death in the Bhandup fatality case.Police said Thite alighted from a train on platform 4, jumped onto the tracks and was attempting to reach platform 3 to board another local when a fast train hit him. He was rushed to a public hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries.Police said they have gone through CCTV footage but are yet to establish the circumstances that led him to cross the tracks.
Article Summary: A 21-year-old Mulund resident, Sahil Thite, died after being hit by a local train while crossing the tracks at Bhandup station. Two people were found dead on tracks between Ghatkopar and Vikhroli stations Monday evening. The disruption affected thousands of commuters, stranded passengers in stationary trains for up to 90 minutes.

Article Title: 'Scaled boundary wall to enter': 40 minor girls at Rajasthan tribal hostel 'molested, abused' by coach's husband
Article Text:
Around 40 students from the Govt Tribal Girls Ashram Hostel have reported repeated harassment by Premshankar Meena, the husband of their sports coach (Representative image)





KOTA: Around 40 students of Govt Tribal Girls Ashram Hostel at Pachhad in Baran district have written to SP Abhishek Andasu alleging molestation, repeated harassment and verbal abuse by the husband of a sports coach, who they claim makes frequent unauthorized visits to the hostel premises.The students, all of them minors, along with hostel superintendent Mamta Gautam, formally approached the SP Sunday, seeking urgent intervention and legal action against the accused, identified as Premshankar Meena, husband of coach Ramsarekha Bai.According to complaints submitted separately by students and the hostel superintendent, copies of which are with TOI, Meena routinely enters the hostel, often in an inebriated state, before proceeding to molest, harass and verbally abuse minor students.An already distressing situation escalated last Saturday night, when Meena allegedly scaled the hostel's boundary wall and entered the premises unlawfully around 8pm. Once inside, he molested several girls and used foul language, the complaints state.The students claimed this last incident in particular affected the hostel's atmosphere.Hostel authorities said they tried to report Saturday’s incident to Chhipabarod police station immediately, but no action was initiated.Fearing for their safety and frustrated by the lack of response from police, the students and hostel superintendent decided to approach the Baran SP directly, demanding legal action against Meena and steps to restore a secure environment at the hostel.Some of the complainants also shared a video they claimed documents their allegations and added that Meena’s actions have created fear among them.Baran SP Andasu, ASP Sourabh Tiwari, Chhipabarod area DSP Tarachand and circle inspector Gambhir Singh did not respond to repeated calls seeking their responses to the matter.
Article Summary: Around 40 students of Govt Tribal Girls Ashram Hostel at Pachhad in Baran district have written to SP Abhishek Andasu alleging molestation, repeated harassment and verbal abuse. The students, all of them minors, along with hostel superintendent Mamta Gautam, formally approached the SP Sunday. Accused is Premshankar Meena, husband of coach Ramsarekha Bai.

Article Title: Bengal Class 11 student rape-murder accused killed in encounter during crime scene reconstruction
Article Text:
A 23-year-old man named Prahlad Das, accused of raping and murdering a teenager, was killed in an encounter.





KOLKATA: The 23-year-old man arrested for the alleged rape and murder of a 17-year-old Class 11 student in West Bengal’s North 24 Parganas district was killed in a police encounter early Tuesday, police sources said.The accused, Prahlad Das, allegedly snatched a service revolver during the reconstruction of the crime scene in Bongaon between 3am and 3.30am, fired at police personnel and jumped into a pond in an attempt to escape, according to police sources.Police opened fire in self-defence. He was rushed to a hospital, where he was declared dead.The accused’s death comes two days after the girl’s body was recovered from behind a house in Gaighata, near the Indo-Bangladesh border, on Sunday morning.The teenager had allegedly gone missing on Saturday night after attending a musical programme near a local market.According to the police, the girl, who lived with her maternal grandparents, had left the programme after receiving a phone call. Her family members and neighbours searched for her through the night before locals found her body in the backyard of a relative’s house.The body bore multiple injuries, including marks on the head and face, preliminary findings indicated.A post-mortem examination was ordered as part of the investigation.Police had arrested Das, a resident of Shimulpur in Gaighata who was reportedly known to the victim, on the basis of a complaint lodged by her family. A Bongaon court had remanded him in 10 days of police custody on Sunday.Bongaon Police District SP Bidisha Kalita Dasgupta had said a special investigation team led by the area’s additional superintendent of police was formed to probe the case. Investigators were also examining whether others were involved in the crime.Preliminary questioning had suggested that the accused allegedly harboured resentment towards the girl over remarks she had made about his mother, police said, adding that the motive and possible involvement of others were being investigated.The incident had triggered protests in the area, prompting the deployment of a large police contingent, including Rapid Action Force and Combat Force personnel, to maintain law and order.
Article Summary: Prahlad Das, 23, allegedly snatched a service revolver during the reconstruction of the crime scene in Bongaon. He fired at police personnel and jumped into a pond in an attempt to escape, according to police sources. He was rushed to a hospital, where he was declared dead.
